edition_note: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed. (Cambridge, 2013), from pdftotext -layout of the published PDF; pages are printed book pages. Part 1 of the index: chapters 0–3 only (chapters 4–8 are indexed separately). Chapter 0 is a review chapter without numbered theorems: its numbered subsections are listed as §0.x.y (and §0.5, §0.10, §0.11). HJ numbers theorems, definitions, examples and displayed equations on one counter, so gaps in the numbering are equations or examples; examples are included (label Ex) only when they carry a named classical result. Labels with four components (e.g. Thm 2.4.3.2) are as printed. 'Definitions 1.3.16' and 'Definitions 1.4.4' are listed as Def. There is no Corollary 3.5.5 in this edition (3.5.5 is an Example); the LDU/LU-existence corollary is Cor 3.5.6. Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed. (Cambridge, 2013); this file indexes Chapters 4–8 (Chapters 0–3 are indexed separately). Page numbers are the printed pages. Numbering follows the book: theorems, corollaries, lemmas, definitions, observations and displayed equations share one counter per section, so gaps in the labels are equations, examples or exercises. Section 7.4 uses four-level labels (e.g. Thm 7.4.1.1); its unnumbered subsections 7.4.2–7.4.6 and 7.4.12, and the unnumbered Section 5.8, are indexed with § labels because they contain standard results (Eckart–Young, least squares, Procrustes, Kantorovich). Three statements are labelled unusually in the text and are indexed as Lem 7.8.15 (label split across lines), Thm 7.5.7 ('Weak minimum principle 7.5.7') and Thm 7.5.8 ('Fejér's uniqueness theorem 7.5.8'); 'Application 7.5.5', the 4.0.x/5.0.x examples and the (8.1.x) displayed facts are not indexed. Status 'nlalib' for a complex Hermitian statement means NLAlib proves it for real symmetric matrices (and sometimes also complex); equality and strictness clauses are tracked, so a result whose inequalities are proved but whose equality cases are not is 'partial'.

items.name: Scalar field
items.statement: Vector spaces are taken over a field, here usually $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$.

items.name: Vector space
items.statement: Axioms of a vector space over a field; $\mathbb F^n$ and $M_{m,n}(\mathbb F)$ are the main examples.

items.name: Subspace, span
items.statement: Subspaces, linear combinations and the span of a set; the span is the smallest subspace containing the set.

items.name: Linear independence
items.statement: A finite list is linearly independent when only the trivial combination vanishes.

items.name: Basis
items.statement: A linearly independent spanning list; every vector has unique coordinates.

items.name: Extension to a basis
items.statement: Every independent list in a finite-dimensional space extends to a basis.

items.name: Dimension
items.statement: All bases have the same length, the dimension; subspaces have dimension at most that of the space.

items.name: Isomorphism
items.statement: Finite-dimensional spaces over the same field are isomorphic iff they have equal dimension.

items.name: Rectangular arrays
items.statement: An $m\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb F$; notation $M_{m,n}(\mathbb F)$, $M_n$.

items.name: Linear transformations
items.statement: After choosing bases, linear maps between finite-dimensional spaces correspond bijectively to matrices.

items.name: Range and null space
items.statement: Range and null space of a matrix; rank plus nullity equals the number of columns.

items.name: Matrix operations
items.statement: Entrywise sum, scalar multiple and the matrix product (composition of maps).

items.name: Transpose, conjugate transpose, trace
items.statement: Definitions of $A^T$, $A^*$, $\operatorname{tr}A$, and $\operatorname{tr}AB=\operatorname{tr}BA$.

items.name: Metamechanics of multiplication
items.statement: Products as combinations of columns or rows, and $AB$ as a sum of outer products of columns of $A$ with rows of $B$.

items.name: Column and row space
items.statement: The range of $A$ is the span of its columns; row space is the range of $A^T$.

items.name: All-ones matrix and vector
items.statement: Notation $e$ and $J_n=ee^T$ for the all-ones vector and matrix.
items.note: notation only, no statement

items.name: Laplace expansion along a row or column
items.statement: The determinant is the cofactor expansion along any row or column.

items.name: Permutation expansion
items.statement: The determinant is the signed sum over permutations of products of entries.

items.name: Elementary row and column operations
items.statement: The three elementary operations are multiplication by elementary matrices and change the determinant in known ways.

items.name: Reduced row echelon form
items.statement: Every matrix is row equivalent to a unique reduced row echelon form.
items.note: Mathlib defines RREF and pivots; existence/uniqueness of the RREF of a given matrix not checked

items.name: Multiplicativity
items.statement: $\det(AB)=\det A\det B$ for square $A,B$.

items.name: Functional characterization of det
items.statement: det is the unique alternating multilinear function of the rows with $\det I=1$.

items.name: Rank
items.statement: rank $A$ = dimension of the range = number of independent columns.

items.name: Rank and linear systems
items.statement: $Ax=b$ is solvable iff $\operatorname{rank}[A\ b]=\operatorname{rank}A$; solution set is an affine translate of the null space.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `rank-inequalities`; consistency criterion used by Kaczmarz/least-squares consistency hypotheses

items.name: RREF and rank
items.statement: Elementary operations preserve rank; rank is the number of nonzero rows of the RREF.

items.name: Characterizations of rank
items.statement: Equivalent descriptions of rank $k$: $k$ independent rows/columns, a nonsingular $k\times k$ submatrix and none larger, $\dim$ range $=k$, factorization $A=XY^T$ with $k$ columns.
items.note: the largest-nonsingular-submatrix characterization is not stated in Mathlib

items.name: Rank inequalities
items.statement: rank $\le\min(m,n)$; subadditivity; $\operatorname{rank}AB\le\min$; Sylvester $\operatorname{rank}A+\operatorname{rank}B-n\le\operatorname{rank}AB$; Frobenius inequality.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `rank-inequalities`; Mathlib has Matrix.rank_mul_le and Matrix.rank_add_rank_le_card_of_mul_eq_zero only; Sylvester/Frobenius/subadditivity for matrices missing

items.name: Rank equalities
items.statement: $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}A^T=\operatorname{rank}A^*=\operatorname{rank}A^*A=\operatorname{rank}AA^*$; nonsingular factors do not change rank.

items.name: Nonsingularity
items.statement: For square $A$: invertible iff $\det A\ne0$ iff $Ax=0$ only for $x=0$; a one-sided inverse is two-sided.

items.name: Euclidean inner product and norm
items.statement: $\langle x,y\rangle=y^*x$ and $\Vert x\Vert _2=\langle x,x\rangle^{1/2}$.

items.name: Orthogonality and orthonormality
items.statement: Orthogonal and orthonormal vectors and lists.

items.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
items.statement: $\vert \langle x,y\rangle\vert \le\Vert x\Vert \Vert y\Vert $ with equality iff dependent.

items.name: Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization
items.statement: Any independent list can be orthonormalized so that the first $k$ vectors span the same space for each $k$.
items.note: matrix (QR) form in NLAlib; abstract form in Mathlib

items.name: Orthonormal bases
items.statement: Every orthonormal list in $\mathbb C^n$ extends to an orthonormal basis; coordinates are inner products.

items.name: Orthogonal complements
items.statement: $S^\perp$ is a subspace with $\dim S+\dim S^\perp=n$ and $(S^\perp)^\perp=\operatorname{span}S$.

items.name: Submatrices
items.statement: Submatrix $A[\alpha,\beta]$ on index sets; principal and leading principal submatrices.

items.name: Block multiplication
items.statement: Conformally partitioned matrices multiply blockwise.

items.name: Inverse of a partitioned matrix
items.statement: Block formula for the inverse of a $2\times2$ block matrix via Schur complements.

items.name: Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury
items.statement: $(A+XRY)^{-1}=A^{-1}-A^{-1}X(R^{-1}+YA^{-1}X)^{-1}YA^{-1}$ when the inverses exist.

items.name: Complementary nullities
items.statement: For nonsingular $A$: nullity $A[\alpha,\beta]$ = nullity $A^{-1}[\beta^c,\alpha^c]$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `complementary-nullities`

items.name: Rank in a partitioned matrix
items.statement: Rank of a $2\times2$ block matrix in terms of a nonsingular block and its Schur complement; rank-principal matrices.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `complementary-nullities`; rank additivity of the Schur complement; low priority

items.name: Commuting with a block scalar matrix
items.statement: $B$ commutes with $\lambda_1I\oplus\cdots\oplus\lambda_sI$ (distinct $\lambda_i$) iff $B$ is block diagonal conformally.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `sylvester-equation`; special case of the Sylvester-equation uniqueness

items.name: The vec mapping
items.statement: vec stacks columns; $\operatorname{vec}(AXB)=(B^T\otimes A)\operatorname{vec}X$.

items.name: Compound matrices
items.statement: The $r$-th compound collects all $r\times r$ minors; it is multiplicative (Cauchy–Binet).
items.note: proposed atlas entry `cauchy-binet`

items.name: Adjugate and inverse
items.statement: $A\operatorname{adj}A=(\det A)I$, so $A^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}A/\det A$; rank of the adjugate.
items.note: rank-of-adjugate facts not checked

items.name: Cramer's rule
items.statement: Components of $A^{-1}b$ as ratios of determinants.

items.name: Minors of the inverse (Jacobi)
items.statement: $\det A^{-1}[\alpha^c,\beta^c]=\pm\det A[\beta,\alpha]/\det A$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `complementary-nullities`

items.name: Schur complements and determinant formulae
items.statement: $\det\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}=\det A\det(D-CA^{-1}B)$; bordered determinants and $\det(A+xy^T)$.

items.name: Determinantal identities of Sylvester and Kronecker
items.statement: Sylvester's identity for bordered minors; Kronecker's theorem on rank via bordered minors.
items.note: classical determinant identities with no randomized-NLA consumer

items.name: Cauchy–Binet formula
items.statement: $\det(AB)[\alpha,\beta]=\sum_\gamma\det A[\alpha,\gamma]\det B[\gamma,\beta]$; in particular $\det(A^TA)=\sum_S\det(A_S)^2$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `cauchy-binet`; absent from Mathlib and NLAlib; consumer: volume sampling normalisers

items.name: Relations among minors
items.statement: Quadratic (Plücker-type) relations among the maximal minors of a matrix.
items.note: Plücker relations; no consumer

items.name: Laplace expansion theorem
items.statement: Generalized Laplace expansion of det along a set of $k$ rows.
items.note: generalized Laplace expansion; Mathlib has the row case (Matrix.det_succ_row); no consumer for the general form

items.name: Derivative of the determinant
items.statement: $\tfrac{d}{dt}\det A(t)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}A(t)A'(t))$ (Jacobi's formula), and the derivative of the characteristic polynomial is the sum of principal $(n-1)$-minors.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `determinant-derivative`

items.name: Dodgson's identity
items.statement: Desnanot–Jacobi condensation identity for $\det A$.
items.note: determinant condensation; no consumer

items.name: Adjugates and compounds
items.statement: Higher adjugates and their relation to compound matrices.
items.note: exterior-power bookkeeping; no consumer

items.name: Diagonal matrices
items.statement: Diagonal matrices, their products and inverses; left/right multiplication scales rows/columns.

items.name: Block diagonal matrices and direct sums
items.statement: Direct sums $A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus A_k$; det and rank are multiplicative/additive over summands.

items.name: Triangular matrices
items.statement: Upper/lower triangular matrices are closed under products and inverses; det is the product of the diagonal.

items.name: Block triangular matrices
items.statement: Block triangular matrices; det and eigenvalues come from the diagonal blocks.

items.name: Permutation matrices
items.statement: Permutation matrices are real orthogonal; $P^TAP$ permutes rows and columns.

items.name: Circulant matrices
items.statement: Circulants are polynomials in the cyclic shift and commute with each other.

items.name: Toeplitz matrices
items.statement: Matrices constant along diagonals, $a_{ij}=a_{j-i}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `structured-matrices-def`

items.name: Hankel matrices
items.statement: Matrices constant along anti-diagonals, $a_{ij}=a_{i+j}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `structured-matrices-def`

items.name: Hessenberg matrices
items.statement: Upper Hessenberg: $a_{ij}=0$ for $i>j+1$; unreduced if the subdiagonal is nonzero.

items.name: Tridiagonal, bidiagonal and banded matrices
items.statement: Tridiagonal, bidiagonal and banded patterns; Jacobi matrices.
items.note: bidiagonal pattern appears via golub-kahan-bidiagonalization

items.name: Vandermonde matrices and Lagrange interpolation
items.statement: $\det V=\prod_{i<j}(x_j-x_i)$; nonsingularity gives unique polynomial interpolation.

items.name: Cauchy matrices
items.statement: $[1/(a_i+b_j)]$ has a product determinant formula; Hilbert matrix as special case.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `structured-matrices-def`; low priority

items.name: Involution, nilpotent, projection, coninvolution
items.note: coninvolution has no Mathlib name and no consumer

items.name: Change of basis
items.statement: Matrices of a linear map in two bases are similar via the change-of-basis matrix.

items.name: Equivalence relations
items.statement: Reflexive, symmetric, transitive relations partition a set into classes.
items.note: set-theoretic preliminaries (Mathlib Equivalence)

items.label: Def 1.1.2
items.name: Eigenvalue, eigenvector
items.statement: $\lambda,x$ is an eigenpair of $A\in M_n$ if $Ax=\lambda x$ with $x\ne0$.

items.label: Def 1.1.4
items.name: Spectrum
items.statement: $\sigma(A)$ is the set of eigenvalues of $A$.

items.label: Thm 1.1.6
items.name: Eigenvalues of p(A)
items.statement: If $Ax=\lambda x$ then $p(A)x=p(\lambda)x$; conversely every eigenvalue of $p(A)$ ($\deg p\ge1$) is $p(\lambda)$ for some $\lambda\in\sigma(A)$.

items.label: Obs 1.1.7
items.statement: $A$ is singular iff $0\in\sigma(A)$.

items.label: Obs 1.1.8
items.statement: $\lambda\in\sigma(A)$ iff $\lambda+\mu\in\sigma(A+\mu I)$.

items.label: Thm 1.1.9
items.name: Existence of an eigenvalue
items.statement: Every $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ has an eigenvalue; for each $y\ne0$ some polynomial $g$ of degree $\le n-1$ makes $g(A)y$ an eigenvector.
items.note: the Krylov-polynomial refinement is not stated; NLAlib krylov-grade has the related Krylov structure

items.label: Def 1.2.3
items.name: Characteristic polynomial
items.statement: $p_A(t)=\det(tI-A)$.

items.label: Obs 1.2.4
items.statement: $p_A$ is monic of degree $n$ with $t^{n-1}$ coefficient $-\operatorname{tr}A$ and constant term $(-1)^n\det A$; its roots are exactly the eigenvalues.

items.label: Def 1.2.5
items.name: Algebraic multiplicity
items.statement: The multiplicity of $\lambda$ as a root of $p_A$.

items.label: Ex 1.2.7
items.name: det(I + xy*)
items.statement: $I+xy^*$ has eigenvalues $1+y^*x$ and $1$ (multiplicity $n-1$), so $\det(I+xy^*)=1+y^*x$.

items.label: Ex 1.2.8
items.name: Brauer's theorem
items.statement: If $Ax=\lambda x$ and $\sigma(A)=\{\lambda,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n\}$ then $\sigma(A+xy^*)=\{\lambda+y^*x,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n\}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `rank-one-eigenvalue-update`

items.label: Def 1.2.9
items.name: Spectral radius
items.statement: $\rho(A)=\max\{\vert \lambda\vert :\lambda\in\sigma(A)\}$.

items.label: Def 1.2.10
items.name: Principal minor sums
items.statement: $E_k(A)$ is the sum of the $\binom nk$ principal minors of size $k$.
items.note: no named $E_k$; the sum appears inline in NLAlib's volume-sampling identities

items.label: Def 1.2.14
items.name: Elementary symmetric functions
items.statement: $S_k(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is the sum of all products of $k$ distinct $\lambda_i$.

items.label: Thm 1.2.16
items.statement: $S_k(\sigma(A))=E_k(A)$ for every $A\in M_n$ and $k=1,\dots,n$.
items.note: NLAlib has the Hermitian / orthogonally diagonalizable case; general (non-normal) A missing

items.label: Thm 1.2.17
items.statement: For some $\delta>0$, $A+\varepsilon I$ is nonsingular whenever $0<\vert \varepsilon\vert <\delta$.
items.note: one-line consequence of Matrix.finite_spectrum; would not be stated separately

items.label: Thm 1.2.18
items.statement: If $\lambda$ has algebraic multiplicity $k$ then $\operatorname{rank}(A-\lambda I)\ge n-k$, with equality when $k=1$.
items.note: stated as geometric ≤ algebraic multiplicity (equivalent by rank–nullity)

items.label: Def 1.3.1
items.name: Similarity
items.statement: $B$ is similar to $A$ if $B=S^{-1}AS$ for nonsingular $S$; permutation similarity when $S$ is a permutation.
items.note: IsConj in the monoid of matrices (conjugation by units)

items.label: Obs 1.3.2
items.statement: Similarity is an equivalence relation.

items.label: Thm 1.3.3
items.statement: Similar matrices have the same characteristic polynomial.

items.label: Cor 1.3.4
items.statement: Similar matrices have the same eigenvalues; a diagonal matrix similar to $A$ displays its eigenvalues; only $0$ is similar to $0$ and only $I$ to $I$.

items.label: Def 1.3.6
items.name: Diagonalizable
items.statement: $A$ is diagonalizable if it is similar to a diagonal matrix.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`; Mathlib has no matrix diagonalisability predicate (Module.End.IsSemisimple is the abstract analogue over ℂ)

items.label: Thm 1.3.7
items.statement: $A$ is similar to $\begin{pmatrix}\Lambda&C\\0&D\end{pmatrix}$ with $\Lambda$ diagonal $k\times k$ iff $A$ has $k$ independent eigenvectors; diagonalizable iff $n$ independent eigenvectors.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`

items.label: Lem 1.3.8
items.statement: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

items.label: Thm 1.3.9
items.statement: A matrix with $n$ distinct eigenvalues is diagonalizable.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`

items.label: Lem 1.3.10
items.statement: A direct sum is diagonalizable iff each summand is.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`; low priority

items.label: Def 1.3.11
items.name: Simultaneously diagonalizable
items.statement: $A,B$ are simultaneously diagonalizable if one $S$ diagonalizes both.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 1.3.12
items.statement: Diagonalizable $A,B$ commute iff they are simultaneously diagonalizable.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`; Mathlib has the commuting symmetric (orthogonal) case: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSum_isInternal_of_pairwise_commute

items.label: Def 1.3.16
items.name: Commuting family, invariant subspace, reducible family
items.statement: Families of matrices, commuting families, $A$- and $\mathcal F$-invariant subspaces, reducible and irreducible families.

items.label: Obs 1.3.18
items.statement: $A$ is similar to a nontrivial block triangular matrix iff it has a nontrivial invariant subspace; every nonzero invariant subspace contains an eigenvector.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Lem 1.3.19
items.statement: A commuting family has a common eigenvector.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Def 1.3.20
items.statement: A family is simultaneously diagonalizable if a single $S$ diagonalizes every member.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 1.3.21
items.statement: A family of diagonalizable matrices commutes iff it is simultaneously diagonalizable, with any prescribed eigenvalue order for one member.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 1.3.22
items.name: Eigenvalues of AB and BA
items.statement: For $A\in M_{m,n}$, $B\in M_{n,m}$, $m\le n$: $p_{BA}(t)=t^{n-m}p_{AB}(t)$; if $m=n$ and one factor is nonsingular, $AB$ and $BA$ are similar.

items.label: Ex 1.3.23
items.name: Eigenvalues of a low-rank matrix
items.statement: If $A=XY^T$ with $X,Y\in M_{n,r}$ then $\sigma(A)$ is $\sigma(Y^TX)$ together with $n-r$ zeros.

items.label: Ex 1.3.24
items.name: Cauchy's determinant identity
items.statement: $\det(A+xy^T)=\det A\,(1+y^TA^{-1}x)$ for nonsingular $A$.

items.label: Thm 1.3.27
items.statement: Two diagonalizations $A=S\Lambda S^{-1}=T\Lambda T^{-1}$ differ by a block-diagonal factor on the eigenspaces; equivalently corresponding column blocks span the same eigenspaces.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`

items.label: Lem 1.3.28
items.statement: If $S=C+iD$ ($C,D$ real) is nonsingular, some real $C+\tau D$ is nonsingular.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `real-similarity-descent`

items.label: Thm 1.3.29
items.statement: Real families similar over $\mathbb C$ via a common $S$ are similar via a common real $T$; real matrices similar over $\mathbb C$ are similar over $\mathbb R$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `real-similarity-descent`

items.label: Cor 1.3.30
items.statement: Real diagonalizable matrices with real eigenvalues commute iff they are simultaneously diagonalizable by a real similarity.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 1.3.31
items.name: Mirsky
items.statement: Some $A\in M_n$ has prescribed eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ and diagonal $d_i$ iff $\sum\lambda_i=\sum d_i$ (real version too).
items.note: inverse eigenvalue problem for general matrices; the Hermitian analogue is atlas schur-horn

items.label: Obs 1.4.1
items.statement: $A$ and $A^T$ have the same eigenvalues; those of $A^*$ are the conjugates.

items.label: Def 1.4.2
items.name: Eigenspace
items.statement: The eigenspace of $\lambda$ is the null space of $A-\lambda I$.

items.label: Def 1.4.3
items.name: Geometric multiplicity; simple, semisimple eigenvalues
items.statement: Geometric multiplicity = dim of the eigenspace; simple if algebraic multiplicity 1, semisimple if both multiplicities agree.
items.note: no named 'semisimple eigenvalue' predicate

items.label: Def 1.4.4
items.name: Defective, nonderogatory
items.statement: Defective: some geometric < algebraic multiplicity; nonderogatory: every eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity 1.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`

items.label: Def 1.4.6
items.name: Left eigenvector
items.statement: $y\ne0$ with $y^*A=\lambda y^*$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`

items.label: Obs 1.4.6a
items.statement: If $Ax=\lambda x$ and $x^*A=\mu x^*$ then $\lambda=\mu$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`

items.label: Thm 1.4.7
items.name: Biorthogonality
items.statement: Left and right eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal; if $y^*x\ne0$ for the same $\lambda$, $A$ is similar to $[\lambda]\oplus B$ via $S=[x\ S_1]$ with $S^{-*}$ having first column $y/(x^*y)$, and conversely.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`

items.label: Thm 1.4.9
items.statement: If $B=S^{-1}AS$, right eigenvectors map by $S$ and left eigenvectors by $S^{-*}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`; routine

items.label: Thm 1.4.10
items.statement: Geometric multiplicity $\ge k$ ⇒ $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of every principal submatrix of size $\ge n-k+1$ ⇒ algebraic multiplicity $\ge k$; in particular geometric ≤ algebraic.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `diagonalizable-def`; Mathlib has only the 'in particular' (LinearMap.finrank_eigenspace_le); the principal-submatrix chain is not stated

items.label: Lem 1.4.11
items.statement: If $\lambda$ has geometric multiplicity 1 with right/left eigenvectors $x,y$, then $\operatorname{adj}(\lambda I-A)=\gamma xy^*$ for some $\gamma\ne0$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`

items.label: Thm 1.4.12
items.statement: A simple eigenvalue has $y^*x\ne0$; for geometric multiplicity 1, $\lambda$ is simple iff $y^*x\ne0$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`

items.label: Def 2.1.1
items.name: Orthogonal, orthonormal lists
items.statement: $x_i^*x_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, normalized if also $x_i^*x_i=1$.

items.label: Thm 2.1.2
items.statement: An orthonormal list is linearly independent.

items.label: Def 2.1.3
items.name: Unitary, real orthogonal
items.statement: $U^*U=I$; real orthogonal if real with $U^TU=I$.

items.label: Thm 2.1.4
items.name: Characterizations of unitary matrices
items.statement: $U^*U=I$ ⇔ $U^{-1}=U^*$ ⇔ $UU^*=I$ ⇔ orthonormal columns ⇔ orthonormal rows ⇔ $\Vert Ux\Vert _2=\Vert x\Vert _2$ for all $x$.
items.note: the isometry direction (g)⇒(a) is not stated as such

items.label: Def 2.1.5
items.name: Euclidean isometry
items.statement: A linear map preserving the Euclidean norm.

items.label: Obs 2.1.6
items.statement: Products of unitary (real orthogonal) matrices are unitary (real orthogonal).

items.label: Obs 2.1.7
items.statement: The unitary (real orthogonal) matrices form a group.

items.label: Lem 2.1.8
items.name: Selection principle
items.statement: Every sequence of unitary matrices has a subsequence converging to a unitary matrix.
items.note: NLAlib has the real Stiefel set closed and bounded; compactness / subsequence extraction not stated

items.label: Thm 2.1.9
items.statement: For nonsingular $A$: $A^{-1}$ is similar to $A^*$ iff $A=B^{-1}B^*$ for some nonsingular $B$.
items.note: structure result with no consumer

items.label: Lem 2.1.10
items.statement: For unitary $U=[U_{ij}]$ with $U_{11}\in M_k$: $\operatorname{rank}U_{12}=\operatorname{rank}U_{21}$ and $\operatorname{rank}U_{22}=\operatorname{rank}U_{11}+n-2k$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `cs-decomposition`

items.label: Ex 2.1.11
items.name: Plane rotations
items.statement: Plane (Givens) rotations $U(\theta;i,j)$ are real orthogonal and act on two coordinates.

items.label: Ex 2.1.12
items.name: Householder matrices
items.statement: $U_w=I-2ww^*/w^*w$ is unitary, Hermitian and involutory.

items.label: Thm 2.1.13
items.name: Householder map of x to y
items.statement: If $\Vert x\Vert _2=\Vert y\Vert _2>0$ there is an essentially Hermitian unitary $U(y,x)$ (a scaled Householder matrix) with $U(y,x)x=y$ that maps $x^\perp$ into $y^\perp$; real orthogonal for real data.
items.note: NLAlib states the case $y=\mp\Vert x\Vert e_1$ and the general reflection formula; arbitrary $y$ of equal norm not stated

items.label: Thm 2.1.14
items.name: QR factorization
items.statement: Every $A\in M_{n,m}$, $n\ge m$, is $QR$ with orthonormal-column $Q$ and upper triangular $R\ge0$ on the diagonal; unique with $R_{ii}>0$ when rank $A=m$; full form with unitary $Q$.
items.note: real matrices

items.label: Thm 2.1.18
items.statement: Two $n\times k$ matrices with orthonormal columns satisfy $Y=UX$ for some unitary (real orthogonal if real) $U$.
items.note: real case

items.label: Def 2.2.1
items.name: Unitary similarity
items.statement: $A=UBU^*$ with $U$ unitary; unitarily (orthogonally) diagonalizable.
items.note: no named predicate; expressed as conjugation by Matrix.unitaryGroup

items.label: Thm 2.2.2
items.name: Unitary invariance of the Frobenius norm
items.statement: If $A=UBV$ with $U,V$ unitary then $\sum\vert a_{ij}\vert ^2=\sum\vert b_{ij}\vert ^2$.

items.label: Ex 2.2.4
items.name: Unitary reduction to Hessenberg form
items.statement: Every $A$ is unitarily similar (via Householder steps) to an upper Hessenberg matrix with nonnegative subdiagonal.
items.note: existence theorem currently stated with a sorry (atlas formalization status 'stated')

items.label: Thm 2.2.6
items.name: Specht
items.statement: $A,B$ are unitarily similar iff $\operatorname{tr}W(A,A^*)=\operatorname{tr}W(B,B^*)$ for every word $W$.
items.note: unitary-similarity invariants; no consumer

items.label: Thm 2.2.8
items.name: Pearcy
items.statement: Specht's criterion needs only words of bounded length; explicit word lists for $n=2,3,4$.
items.note: unitary-similarity invariants; no consumer

items.label: Thm 2.3.1
items.name: Schur triangularization
items.statement: Every $A\in M_n$ is unitarily similar to an upper triangular $T$ with its eigenvalues on the diagonal in any prescribed order; real orthogonal similarity if $A$ is real with real eigenvalues.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`; not in Mathlib (only abstract triangularizability) or NLAlib

items.label: Ex 2.3.2
items.name: Schur's inequality
items.statement: $\sum_i\vert \lambda_i\vert ^2=\Vert A\Vert _F^2-\sum_{i<j}\vert t_{ij}\vert ^2\le\Vert A\Vert _F^2$, with equality iff $A$ is normal; the strictly upper part of a Schur form is not unique.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`

items.label: Thm 2.3.3
items.statement: A commuting family is simultaneously unitarily upper triangularizable.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 2.3.4
items.name: Real Schur form
items.statement: Every real $A$ is real orthogonally similar to a real upper quasitriangular matrix with $1\times1$ and $2\times2$ diagonal blocks displaying the real eigenvalues and the conjugate pairs.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`

items.label: Thm 2.3.6
items.statement: Commuting real families are simultaneously real quasitriangularizable.
items.note: simultaneous real quasitriangular forms; no consumer

items.label: Cor 2.3.7
items.statement: If $A\bar A=\bar AA$, $A$ is real orthogonally similar to a complex quasitriangular form.
items.note: complex-symmetric / conjugate-linear structure (A Ā, Takagi, coninvolutory); no real-matrix consumer

items.label: Lem 2.4.3.1
items.statement: Product lemma for upper triangular matrices with leading zero blocks (used for Cayley–Hamilton).
items.note: proof-internal lemma; Cayley–Hamilton itself is Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly

items.label: Cor 2.4.3.4
items.statement: For nonsingular $A$, $A^{-1}$ is a polynomial in $A$ of degree $\le n-1$ built from $p_A$.
items.note: NLAlib has the vector form $A^{-1}b\in\mathcal K_\nu(A,b)$; the matrix identity $A^{-1}=q(A)$ is not stated

items.label: Lem 2.4.4.0
items.statement: If $AX=XB$ then $g(A)X=Xg(B)$ for every polynomial $g$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `sylvester-equation`

items.label: Thm 2.4.4.1
items.name: Sylvester
items.statement: $AX-XB=C$ has a unique solution for every $C$ iff $\sigma(A)\cap\sigma(B)=\emptyset$ (real data give a real solution).
items.note: proposed atlas entry `sylvester-equation`; absent from Mathlib; NLAlib none

items.label: Cor 2.4.4.2
items.statement: If $AB=CA$ with block diagonal $B,C$ whose off-diagonal block spectra are disjoint, then $A$ is conformally block diagonal.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `sylvester-equation`

items.label: Cor 2.4.4.3
items.statement: If $A=S(A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus A_d)S^{-1}$ with pairwise disjoint spectra, $B$ commutes with $A$ iff $B=S(B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_d)S^{-1}$ with $A_iB_i=B_iA_i$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `sylvester-equation`

items.label: Thm 2.4.5.1
items.statement: Intertwiners of two upper triangular matrices with the same grouped diagonal are block upper triangular, block diagonal if unitary.
items.note: uniqueness bookkeeping for Schur forms; no consumer

items.label: Thm 2.4.6.1
items.name: Block diagonalization by spectral separation
items.statement: $A$ is similar to $T_{11}\oplus\cdots\oplus T_{dd}$, each $T_{ii}$ upper triangular with the single eigenvalue $\lambda_i$ (real similarity for real $A$ with real eigenvalues).
items.note: proposed atlas entry `sylvester-equation`

items.label: Thm 2.4.6.3
items.statement: A commuting family can be simultaneously reduced to triangular block-diagonal form conformal to one member's eigenvalue grouping.
items.note: commuting-family canonical forms; no consumer

items.label: Cor 2.4.6.4
items.statement: A commuting family is simultaneously similar to block diagonal triangular matrices each block having one eigenvalue.
items.note: commuting-family canonical forms; no consumer

items.label: Thm 2.4.7.1
items.name: Diagonalizable matrices are dense
items.statement: Every $A$ is within any $\varepsilon$ in Frobenius norm of a matrix with $n$ distinct eigenvalues.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`

items.label: Thm 2.4.7.2
items.name: Almost diagonalization
items.statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $S$ with $S^{-1}AS$ upper triangular and off-diagonal entries at most $\varepsilon$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`; consumer: $\rho(A)=\inf$ of induced norms

items.label: Thm 2.4.8.1
items.statement: Commuting $A,B$ have orderings of eigenvalues with $\sigma(A+B)=\{\alpha_i+\beta_i\}$ and $\sigma(AB)=\{\alpha_i\beta_i\}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Cor 2.4.8.5
items.statement: If commuting $A,B$ have $\alpha_i\ne-\beta_j$ for all eigenvalues, $A+B$ is nonsingular.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 2.4.8.6
items.statement: Finitely many matrices are simultaneously triangularizable by similarity iff by a unitary similarity.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`

items.label: Thm 2.4.8.7
items.name: McCoy
items.statement: Simultaneous unitary triangularizability ⇔ $p(A_1,\dots,A_m)(A_kA_l-A_lA_k)$ nilpotent for all noncommutative polynomials ⇔ joint eigenvalue ordering for all $p$.
items.note: noncommutative-polynomial criterion; no consumer

items.label: Lem 2.4.8.10
items.statement: Under McCoy's nilpotency hypothesis every nonzero $x$ can be moved by a noncommutative polynomial to a common eigenvector.
items.note: proof-internal for McCoy

items.label: Lem 2.4.9.1
items.statement: For $A_k\to A$ there are unitaries $U_{k_i}\to U$ with $U_{k_i}^*A_{k_i}U_{k_i}$ triangular and converging to a Schur form of $A$.
items.note: proof-internal compactness lemma for Thm 2.4.9.2

items.label: Thm 2.4.9.2
items.name: Continuity of eigenvalues
items.statement: If $A_k\to A$ then the eigenvalues converge up to a permutation: $\min_\pi\max_i\vert \lambda_{\pi(i)}(A_k)-\lambda_i(A)\vert \to0$.
items.note: NLAlib has the Hermitian case quantitatively (Weyl); the general complex case is missing

items.label: Thm 2.4.10.1
items.name: A. Brauer
items.statement: If $Ax=\lambda x$ and $\sigma(A)=\{\lambda,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n\}$, then $\sigma(A+xv^*)=\{\lambda+v^*x,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n\}$ for every $v$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `rank-one-eigenvalue-update`

items.label: Thm 2.4.11.1
items.name: Complete principle of biorthogonality
items.statement: Unitary and nonunitary deflations from a right/left eigenvector pair: $y^*x=0$ for distinct eigenvalues, a $\lambda$ with $y^*x=0$ has algebraic multiplicity $\ge2$, and $y^*x\ne0$ gives a similarity to $[\lambda]\oplus A_{n-1}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `left-right-eigenvectors`

items.label: Def 2.5.1
items.name: Normal matrix
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`; Mathlib has IsStarNormal for star algebras but no matrix spectral theorem for normal matrices

items.label: Lem 2.5.2
items.statement: A block upper triangular matrix is normal iff it is block diagonal with normal blocks; a triangular normal matrix is diagonal.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`

items.label: Thm 2.5.3
items.name: Spectral theorem for normal matrices
items.statement: $A$ is normal ⇔ unitarily diagonalizable ⇔ $\sum\vert a_{ij}\vert ^2=\sum\vert \lambda_i\vert ^2$ ⇔ $A$ has $n$ orthonormal eigenvectors.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`

items.label: Thm 2.5.4
items.statement: Unitary diagonalizations of a normal matrix differ by block unitaries on the eigenspaces; two normal matrices are unitarily similar iff they have the same eigenvalues.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`

items.label: Thm 2.5.5
items.statement: A family of normal matrices commutes iff it is simultaneously unitarily diagonalizable.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `simultaneous-diagonalization`; Mathlib covers the commuting Hermitian case (LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSum_isInternal_of_pairwise_commute)

items.label: Thm 2.5.6
items.name: Spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices
items.statement: A Hermitian matrix has real eigenvalues and $A=U\Lambda U^*$ with $U$ unitary.
items.note: NLAlib restates the real form

items.label: Lem 2.5.7
items.statement: A real normal $2\times2$ matrix with non-real eigenvalues has the form $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`

items.label: Thm 2.5.8
items.name: Real normal form
items.statement: A real normal matrix is real orthogonally similar to a direct sum of $1\times1$ blocks and $2\times2$ blocks $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix}$, determined by the eigenvalues.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`

items.label: Cor 2.5.11
items.name: Real symmetric, skew-symmetric and orthogonal forms
items.statement: Real symmetric ⇔ real orthogonally diagonalizable; real skew-symmetric and real orthogonal matrices have the $2\times2$ block canonical forms; each class is determined up to orthogonal similarity by eigenvalues.
items.note: symmetric case (a) only; skew-symmetric and orthogonal canonical forms missing

items.label: Thm 2.5.15
items.statement: A commuting family of real normal matrices is simultaneously real orthogonally similar to the quasidiagonal form.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`; low priority

items.label: Thm 2.5.16
items.name: Fuglede–Putnam
items.statement: For normal $A,B$: $AX=XB$ iff $A^*X=XB^*$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `normal-matrices`

items.label: Thm 2.5.17
items.statement: For normal $A$: $\bar AA=A\bar A$ ⇔ $A^TA=AA^T$ ⇔ real orthogonal similarity to a direct sum of special blocks.
items.note: complex-symmetric / conjugate-linear structure (A Ā, Takagi, coninvolutory); no real-matrix consumer

items.label: Cor 2.5.18
items.statement: Symmetric unitary matrices are $Q\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\theta})Q^T$ with real orthogonal $Q$; skew-symmetric unitary ones have a $2\times2$ block form.
items.note: complex-symmetric / conjugate-linear structure (A Ā, Takagi, coninvolutory); no real-matrix consumer

items.label: Cor 2.5.20
items.name: QS factorization of a unitary matrix
items.statement: A symmetric unitary has a symmetric unitary square root that is a polynomial in it; every unitary is $QS$ with $Q$ real orthogonal and $S$ symmetric unitary.
items.note: complex-symmetric / conjugate-linear structure (A Ā, Takagi, coninvolutory); no real-matrix consumer

items.label: Thm 2.5.21
items.statement: Real families unitarily similar via a common $U$ are real orthogonally similar via a common $Q$; unitarily similar real matrices are orthogonally similar.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `real-similarity-descent`

items.label: Thm 2.6.1
items.name: Generalized Schur form
items.statement: Any $A,B\in M_n$ are simultaneously unitarily equivalent to upper triangular $T_A,T_B$; for nonsingular $B$ the ratios of diagonals are the eigenvalues of $B^{-1}A$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`; QZ form; low priority

items.label: Thm 2.6.2
items.name: Real generalized Schur form
items.statement: Real $A,B$ are simultaneously real orthogonally equivalent to quasitriangular $T_A$ and triangular $T_B$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `schur-triangularization`; low priority

items.label: Thm 2.6.3
items.name: Singular value decomposition
items.statement: $A=V\Sigma W^*$ with $V,W$ unitary and $\Sigma$ nonnegative diagonal $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_q$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$ of them positive; the $\sigma_i^2$ are the nonzero eigenvalues of $AA^*$ and of $A^*A$.
items.note: real matrices

items.label: Thm 2.6.4
items.name: Continuity of singular values
items.statement: If $A_k\to A$ then $\sigma_i(A_k)\to\sigma_i(A)$ for each $i$.
items.note: NLAlib has the stronger Lipschitz bound $\vert \sigma_i(A+E)-\sigma_i(A)\vert \le\Vert E\Vert $

items.label: Thm 2.6.5
items.name: Autonne's uniqueness theorem
items.statement: Two SVDs $V\Sigma W^*=\hat V\Sigma\hat W^*$ differ by a common block unitary on each distinct positive singular value and arbitrary unitaries on the null parts.
items.note: NLAlib has uniqueness of the singular values only, not of singular subspaces/vectors

items.label: Cor 2.6.6
items.name: Autonne–Takagi
items.statement: Complex symmetric $A=U\Sigma U^T$ with unitary $U$; complex skew-symmetric matrices have a $2\times2$ block analogue.
items.note: complex-symmetric / conjugate-linear structure (A Ā, Takagi, coninvolutory); no real-matrix consumer

items.label: Cor 2.6.7
items.name: Real SVD
items.statement: A real $A$ factors as $P\Sigma Q^T$ with $P,Q$ real orthogonal and $\Sigma$ nonnegative diagonal.

items.label: Thm 2.7.1
items.name: CS decomposition
items.statement: A unitary $U=\begin{pmatrix}U_{11}&U_{12}\\U_{21}&U_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ with $U_{11}\in M_p$, $p\le q$, is block-unitarily equivalent to $\begin{pmatrix}C&S&0\\-S&C&0\\0&0&I\end{pmatrix}$, $C=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i(U_{11}))$, $S=(I-C^2)^{1/2}$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `cs-decomposition`

items.label: Def 3.1.1
items.name: Jordan block, Jordan matrix
items.statement: $J_k(\lambda)$ has $\lambda$ on the diagonal and ones on the superdiagonal; a Jordan matrix is a direct sum of such blocks.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Lem 3.1.4
items.statement: Identities for $J_k(0)$: $J_k(0)^TJ_k(0)=0\oplus I_{k-1}$ and $J_k(0)^p=0$ for $p\ge k$.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.1.5
items.name: Nilpotent Jordan form
items.statement: A strictly upper triangular matrix is similar to a direct sum of nilpotent Jordan blocks (real similarity if real).
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.1.11
items.name: Jordan canonical form
items.statement: Every $A$ is similar to a Jordan matrix unique up to permutation of blocks.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Lem 3.1.18
items.statement: Block counts from the Weyr characteristic; $A,B$ similar iff same eigenvalues and Weyr characteristics.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.1.21
items.statement: For any $\varepsilon\ne0$, $A$ is similar to a Jordan form with superdiagonal entries $\varepsilon$.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.2.3.1
items.statement: Every $A$ is similar to $A^T$ via a complex symmetric similarity.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.2.3.2
items.statement: Every square complex matrix is a product of two complex symmetric matrices, one of them nonsingular.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Def 3.2.4.1
items.name: Nonderogatory
items.statement: Every eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity one.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `companion-matrix`

items.label: Thm 3.2.4.2
items.statement: If $A$ is nonderogatory, every matrix commuting with $A$ is a polynomial in $A$ of degree $\le n-1$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `companion-matrix`; low priority

items.label: Cor 3.2.4.4
items.statement: For nonderogatory $A$, $AB=BA^T$ forces $B$ symmetric, and every similarity $A^T=S^{-1}AS$ is symmetric.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.2.5.2
items.name: Convergent and power-bounded matrices
items.statement: $A^k\to0$ iff $\rho(A)<1$; $\{A^k\}$ is bounded iff $\rho(A)\le1$ and every eigenvalue of modulus one is semisimple.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `matrix-power-convergence`; Mathlib has Gelfand's formula (spectrum.pow_nnnorm_pow_one_div_tendsto_nhds_spectralRadius) but not this statement

items.label: Obs 3.2.9.2
items.statement: A matrix with fewer than $m-1$ nonzero off-diagonal entries is permutation similar to a nontrivial direct sum.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Obs 3.2.9.3
items.statement: Every matrix is permutation similar to a direct sum of permutation-indecomposable matrices.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Obs 3.2.9.4
items.statement: With $p$ nonzero off-diagonal entries, the Jordan form has at least $n-p$ blocks.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.2.9.5
items.name: Optimality of the Jordan form
items.statement: Any matrix similar to $A$ has at least $n-r$ nonzero off-diagonal entries, $r$ the number of Jordan blocks.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.2.10.1
items.statement: The index of $\lambda$ in a block upper triangular matrix is at most the sum of its indices in the diagonal blocks.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.2.10.2
items.statement: For $\begin{pmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\0&\lambda I\end{pmatrix}$ with diagonalizable $A_{11}$, Jordan blocks have size at most 2 (and 1 away from $\lambda$).
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.2.11.1
items.statement: $AB$ and $BA$ have the same Jordan blocks for every nonzero eigenvalue.
items.note: Jordan structure; the eigenvalue statement is Thm 1.3.22 (Matrix.charpoly_mul_comm')

items.label: Def 3.2.12.1
items.name: Drazin inverse
items.statement: From $A=S(B\oplus N)S^{-1}$ with $B$ nonsingular and $N$ nilpotent, $A^D=S(B^{-1}\oplus0)S^{-1}$.
items.note: Drazin inverse; NLAlib uses the Moore–Penrose inverse, no consumer

items.label: Thm 3.2.13.1
items.statement: If $Ax=\lambda x$, $y^*A=\lambda y^*$, $y^*x\ne0$, the Jordan form of $A+xv^*$ replaces $[\lambda]$ by $[\lambda+v^*x]$ when that is not another eigenvalue.
items.note: Jordan-structure refinement of Brauer's theorem (Thm 2.4.10.1)

items.label: Thm 3.3.1
items.statement: There is a unique monic annihilating polynomial $q_A$ of least degree ($\le n$), and it divides every monic annihilating polynomial.

items.label: Def 3.3.2
items.name: Minimal polynomial
items.statement: $q_A$ is the minimal polynomial of $A$.

items.label: Cor 3.3.3
items.statement: Similar matrices have the same minimal polynomial.

items.label: Cor 3.3.4
items.statement: $q_A$ divides $p_A$, and its roots are exactly the eigenvalues.

items.label: Thm 3.3.6
items.statement: $q_A(t)=\prod_i(t-\lambda_i)^{r_i}$ with $r_i$ the largest Jordan block size for $\lambda_i$.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.3.8
items.statement: $A$ is diagonalizable iff $\prod_i(A-\lambda_iI)=0$ over its distinct eigenvalues.
items.note: stated for semisimple endomorphisms (= diagonalizable over ℂ)

items.label: Cor 3.3.10
items.statement: $A$ is diagonalizable iff $q_A$ has distinct linear factors iff every eigenvalue is a simple root of $q_A$.
items.note: stated for semisimple endomorphisms (= diagonalizable over ℂ)

items.label: Def 3.3.13
items.name: Companion matrix
items.statement: The companion matrix of a monic polynomial.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `companion-matrix`

items.label: Thm 3.3.14
items.statement: A monic polynomial is both the minimal and the characteristic polynomial of its companion matrix.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `companion-matrix`

items.label: Thm 3.3.15
items.statement: $\deg q_A=n$ ⇔ $q_A=p_A$ ⇔ $A$ nonderogatory ⇔ $A$ similar to the companion matrix of $p_A$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `companion-matrix`

items.label: Thm 3.4.1.5
items.name: Real Jordan canonical form
items.statement: Every real matrix is real-similar to a direct sum of real Jordan blocks and blocks $C_k(a,b)$ for conjugate pairs.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.4.1.7
items.statement: $A$ is similar to a real matrix iff Jordan blocks for $\lambda$ and $\bar\lambda$ match iff $\operatorname{rank}(A-\lambda I)^k=\operatorname{rank}(A-\bar\lambda I)^k$.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.4.1.8
items.statement: A block triangular matrix with a block similar to a real matrix and zero elsewhere is similar to a real matrix.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.4.1.9
items.statement: $A\bar A$ is similar to $\bar AA$ and to a real matrix.
items.note: complex-symmetric / conjugate-linear structure (A Ā, Takagi, coninvolutory); no real-matrix consumer

items.label: Cor 3.4.1.10
items.statement: A real diagonalizable matrix is real-similar to a direct sum of $2\times2$ blocks $C_1(a,b)$ and its real eigenvalues.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.4.2.3
items.name: Weyr canonical form
items.statement: Every $A$ is similar to a direct sum of Weyr blocks, unique for a given ordering of the eigenvalues.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Lem 3.4.2.4
items.statement: Commutants of upper triangular Weyr-type block matrices are block upper triangular.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.4.2.5
items.name: Belitskii
items.statement: Matrices commuting with a Weyr form are block upper triangular with prescribed block identities.
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.4.2.10
items.statement: Belitskii's theorem and simultaneous Weyr forms for commuting families (O'Meara–Vinsonhaler).
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Thm 3.4.3.1
items.name: Littlewood
items.statement: $A$ is unitarily similar to an upper triangular form whose block structure displays the Weyr characteristic (unitary Weyr form).
items.note: Jordan/Weyr canonical-form theory over C; no randomized-NLA consumer (brief: out of scope)

items.label: Cor 3.4.3.3
items.name: Canonical form of a projection
items.statement: An idempotent $A$ with singular values $\sigma_1\ge\dots\ge\sigma_g>1$ is unitarily similar to a direct sum of blocks $\begin{pmatrix}1&(\sigma_i^2-1)^{1/2}\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, identity and zero blocks.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `cs-decomposition`; gives $\Vert P\Vert =1/\cos\theta_{\max}$ for oblique projectors

items.label: Def 3.5.1
items.name: LU factorization
items.statement: $A=LU$ with $L$ lower and $U$ upper triangular.
items.note: NLAlib's IsLU requires L unit lower triangular (HJ's exercise: equivalent when L is nonsingular)

items.label: Lem 3.5.2
items.statement: In an LU factorization each leading principal block satisfies $A_{11}=L_{11}U_{11}$.
items.note: stated for unit-lower L

items.label: Thm 3.5.3
items.name: Row and column inclusion
items.statement: $A$ has an LU factorization with nonsingular $L$ iff it has the row inclusion property (and dually for nonsingular $U$).
items.note: proposed atlas entry `lu-row-inclusion`; LU of singular matrices; low priority

items.label: Cor 3.5.4
items.statement: If rank $A=k$ and the leading $j\times j$ blocks are nonsingular for $j\le k$, $A$ has an LU factorization, either factor unit triangular; both factors nonsingular iff $k=n$.
items.note: proposed atlas entry `lu-row-inclusion`

items.label: Cor 3.5.6
items.name: LDU factorization
items.statement: Nonsingular $A$ has an LU factorization iff all leading principal minors are nonzero; then $A=LDU$ uniquely with unit triangular $L,U$ and $d_i=\det A_i/\det A_{i-1}$.
items.note: D = diag(U); the pivot formula is IsLU.det_leadingSubmatrix. Atlas and docstrings cite this as 'Cor. 3.5.5' (an Example in the 2nd ed.)

items.label: Lem 3.5.7
items.statement: For nonsingular $A$ some row permutation makes every leading principal minor nonzero.
items.note: follows by combining the two, not stated

items.label: Thm 3.5.8
items.name: PLU factorization
items.statement: Every $A\in M_n$ is $PLU$ with $P$ a permutation, $L$ unit lower and $U$ upper triangular.
items.note: NLAlib's is stronger ($\vert l_{ij}\vert \le1$) and has no invertibility hypothesis

items.label: Thm 3.5.11
items.name: LPU factorization
items.statement: Every $A$ is $LPU$ with $L$ unit lower, $P$ a permutation, $U$ upper triangular; $P$ is unique if $A$ is nonsingular.
items.note: Bruhat-type decomposition; no consumer

items.label: Def 3.5.12
items.name: Triangular equivalence
items.statement: $A=LBU$ with nonsingular lower $L$ and upper $U$.
items.note: Bruhat-type decomposition; no consumer

items.label: Thm 3.5.13
items.statement: Nonsingular $A,B$ are triangularly equivalent iff they share the LPU permutation iff the ranks of all leading $p\times q$ blocks agree.
items.note: Bruhat-type decomposition; no consumer

items.label: Thm 3.5.14
items.name: LPDU factorization
items.statement: Nonsingular $A=LPDU$ with unique $P$ and $D$.
items.note: Bruhat-type decomposition; no consumer

items.label: Def 4.1.1
items.statement: A square complex matrix is Hermitian if $A=A^*$ and skew-Hermitian if $A=-A^*$; sums, powers and inverses of Hermitian matrices stay Hermitian.
items.note: Mathlib `Matrix.IsHermitian`; skew-Hermitian as `skewAdjoint`.

items.label: Thm 4.1.2
items.name: Toeplitz decomposition
items.statement: Every $A\in M_n$ has a unique decomposition $A=H+iK$ with $H,K$ Hermitian, and a unique decomposition $A=H+S$ with $H$ Hermitian and $S$ skew-Hermitian.

items.label: Thm 4.1.3
items.statement: If $A$ is Hermitian then $x^*Ax$ is real for every $x$, all eigenvalues are real, and $S^*AS$ is Hermitian for every $S$.

items.label: Thm 4.1.4
items.statement: A complex matrix is Hermitian iff $x^*Ax$ is real for all $x$, iff it is normal with real eigenvalues, iff $S^*AS$ is Hermitian for all $S$.
items.note: Stated in Mathlib for operators / C*-algebra elements, not as a matrix TFAE.

items.label: Thm 4.1.5
items.name: Spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices
items.statement: A matrix is Hermitian iff it is unitarily diagonalizable with a real diagonal; a real matrix is symmetric iff it is orthogonally diagonalizable.
items.note: Mathlib gives the forward direction for any `RCLike` field (real symmetric included); the converse is immediate.

items.label: Thm 4.1.6
items.statement: A nonempty family of Hermitian matrices is simultaneously unitarily diagonalizable iff its members commute pairwise.
items.note: Mathlib states the joint-eigenspace decomposition for commuting symmetric operators.

items.label: Thm 4.1.7
items.statement: TFAE: $A$ is similar to a real matrix; $A$ is similar to $A^*$ (even via a Hermitian similarity); $A=HK$ with $H,K$ Hermitian (one of them nonsingular).
items.note: Similarity theory over ℂ (Jordan-form based); no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.1.8
items.statement: $x^*Ax$ is real and positive (nonnegative) for all nonzero $x\in\mathbb C^n$ iff $A$ is Hermitian with all eigenvalues positive (nonnegative).

items.label: Def 4.1.9
items.statement: Complex $A$ is positive definite (semidefinite) if $x^*Ax$ is real and positive (nonnegative) for all $x\neq0$; indefinite if $x^*Ax$ takes both signs.
items.note: Indefinite is not a named Mathlib notion.

items.label: Thm 4.1.10
items.statement: A real symmetric matrix satisfies $x^TAx>0$ ($\ge0$) for all real $x\neq0$ iff all its eigenvalues are positive (nonnegative).

items.label: Def 4.1.11
items.statement: Real symmetric $A$ is positive definite (semidefinite) if $x^TAx>0$ ($\ge0$) for all real $x\neq0$; indefinite if both signs occur.

items.label: Def 4.1.12
items.statement: For Hermitian $A=U\Lambda U^*$, the positive and negative parts are $A_\pm=U\Lambda_\pm U^*$ built from $\max(\lambda_i,0)$ and $-\min(\lambda_i,0)$.
items.note: Mathlib defines `a⁺`, `a⁻` through the continuous functional calculus.

items.label: Prop 4.1.13
items.statement: For Hermitian $A$: $A=A_+-A_-$ with $A_\pm\succeq0$, $A_+A_-=A_-A_+=0$, $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}A_++\operatorname{rank}A_-$, and $A_-$ is the positive part of $-A$.
items.note: Rank additivity not found in Mathlib.

items.label: Thm 4.2.2
items.name: Rayleigh quotient theorem
items.statement: For Hermitian $A$ and orthonormal eigenvectors $x_{i_1},\dots,x_{i_k}$ spanning $S$, the Rayleigh quotient on $S$ ranges exactly over $[\lambda_{i_1},\lambda_{i_k}]$; in particular $\lambda_{\min}\le x^*Ax/x^*x\le\lambda_{\max}$.
items.note: Whole-space extrema proved; the version on the span of a chosen set of eigenvectors is not stated.

items.label: Lem 4.2.3
items.name: Subspace intersection lemma
items.statement: If subspaces $S_1,\dots,S_k\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ have $\delta=\sum\dim S_i-(k-1)n\ge1$, their intersection contains $\delta$ orthonormal vectors.
items.note: NLAlib has the two-subspace dimension count; the k-subspace orthonormal form is not stated (Mathlib `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq` gives the dimension formula).

items.label: Lem 4.2.4
items.statement: If $\emptyset\neq S_1\subseteq S_2$ and $f$ is bounded, then $\sup_{S_2}f\ge\sup_{S_1}f\ge\inf_{S_1}f\ge\inf_{S_2}f$.

items.label: Obs 4.2.5
items.statement: The increasingly ordered eigenvalues of $-A$ are $\lambda_k(-A)=-\lambda_{n-k+1}(A)$.
items.note: Not stated in NLAlib or Mathlib; candidate `eigenvalue-order-and-counting`.

items.label: Thm 4.2.6
items.name: Courant–Fischer min-max theorem
items.statement: Courant–Fischer: $\lambda_k=\min_{\dim S=k}\max_{0\ne x\in S}x^*Ax/x^*x=\max_{\dim S=n-k+1}\min_{0\ne x\in S}x^*Ax/x^*x$ for Hermitian $A$.

items.label: Thm 4.2.10
items.statement: If $x^*Ax\ge c$ (resp. $>c$) on the unit sphere of a $k$-dimensional subspace then $\lambda_{n-k+1}(A)\ge c$ (resp. $>c$); dually for $\le c$ and $\lambda_k$.
items.note: Non-strict versions proved (real and complex); the strict-inequality versions are not stated.

items.label: Cor 4.2.12
items.statement: If $x^*Ax\ge0$ (resp. $>0$ for $x\ne0$) on a $k$-dimensional subspace, then $A$ has at least $k$ nonnegative (resp. positive) eigenvalues.
items.note: Nonnegative case is the $c=0$ instance of `le_eigenvalues₀_of_forall_mem`; the counting form and the strict case are not stated (candidate `eigenvalue-order-and-counting`).

items.label: Thm 4.3.1
items.name: Weyl's inequalities
items.statement: Weyl: for Hermitian $A,B$, $\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+j}(A)+\lambda_{n-j}(B)$ and $\lambda_{i-j+1}(A)+\lambda_j(B)\le\lambda_i(A+B)$, with equality iff a common eigenvector exists.
items.note: `eigenvalues₀_add_le` is (4.3.2a) for real symmetric matrices in decreasing order; (4.3.2b) (by negation) and the equality cases are not stated.

items.label: Cor 4.3.3
items.statement: If $B$ has $\pi$ positive and $\nu$ negative eigenvalues then $\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+\pi}(A)$ and $\lambda_{i-\nu}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)$, with stated equality cases.
items.note: Candidate `low-rank-update-interlacing`.

items.label: Cor 4.3.5
items.statement: If $B$ is Hermitian of rank $r$ then $\lambda_{i-r}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+r}(A)$ (interlacing for rank-$r$ perturbations).
items.note: Candidate `low-rank-update-interlacing`; derivable from `eigenvalues₀_add_le` but not stated.

items.label: Cor 4.3.7
items.statement: If $B$ has exactly one positive and one negative eigenvalue then $\lambda_{i-1}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+1}(A)$.
items.note: Candidate `low-rank-update-interlacing`.

items.label: Cor 4.3.9
items.statement: Rank-one updates interlace: $\lambda_i(A)\le\lambda_i(A+zz^*)\le\lambda_{i+1}(A)$ and $\lambda_{i-1}(A)\le\lambda_i(A-zz^*)\le\lambda_i(A)$, strictly if no eigenvector is orthogonal to $z$.
items.note: Candidate `low-rank-update-interlacing`.

items.label: Cor 4.3.12
items.statement: If $B\succeq0$ then $\lambda_i(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)$ for all $i$ (strict if $B\succ0$), with equality characterised.
items.note: Monotonicity proved (real and complex); strict version for $B\succ0$ and equality cases missing.

items.label: Cor 4.3.15
items.statement: For Hermitian $A,B$: $\lambda_i(A)+\lambda_1(B)\le\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_i(A)+\lambda_n(B)$, with equality iff a common eigenvector exists.
items.note: Upper bound is the $j=0$ case of `eigenvalues₀_add_le`; the lower bound and equality cases are not stated (atlas candidate `eigenvalue-perturbation-symmetric`).

items.label: Thm 4.3.17
items.name: Cauchy interlacing theorem
items.statement: Cauchy interlacing: for the bordered Hermitian matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}B&y\\y^*&a\end{bmatrix}$, $\lambda_1(A)\le\lambda_1(B)\le\lambda_2(A)\le\dots\le\lambda_n(B)\le\lambda_{n+1}(A)$, with equality cases.
items.note: Inequalities proved for compressions $Q^TAQ$ (real symmetric), which include principal submatrices; equality and strictness clauses missing.

items.label: Thm 4.3.21
items.statement: Converse of interlacing: if $\mu_1\le\lambda_1\le\mu_2\le\dots\le\lambda_n\le\mu_{n+1}$, there are real $a$ and $y$ with $\begin{bmatrix}\Lambda&y\\y^T&a\end{bmatrix}$ having eigenvalues $\mu_i$.
items.note: Candidate `interlacing-converse` (later).

items.label: Thm 4.3.26
items.statement: If $\lambda_1\le\mu_1\le\lambda_2\le\dots\le\lambda_n\le\mu_n$, there is a real $z$ such that $\Lambda+zz^T$ has eigenvalues $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n$.
items.note: Candidate `interlacing-converse` (later).

items.label: Thm 4.3.28
items.statement: For a Hermitian $A$ with leading $m\times m$ principal block $B$: $\lambda_i(A)\le\lambda_i(B)\le\lambda_{i+n-m}(A)$, with equality characterised via eigenvectors of $B$ annihilated by $C^*$.
items.note: Inequalities proved (compression form); equality analysis (4.3.31) missing.

items.label: Cor 4.3.34
items.statement: The trace of an $m\times m$ principal submatrix lies between the sums of the $m$ smallest and $m$ largest eigenvalues; equality forces a block-diagonal splitting.
items.note: Coordinate-subspace case of the Ky Fan principle; existing atlas candidates.

items.label: Cor 4.3.37
items.name: Poincaré separation theorem
items.statement: Poincaré separation: for orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_m$ and $B_m=[u_i^*Au_j]$, $\lambda_i(A)\le\lambda_i(B_m)\le\lambda_{i+n-m}(A)$.
items.note: Real symmetric form, decreasing indexing.

items.label: Cor 4.3.39
items.name: Ky Fan maximum principle
items.statement: Ky Fan: $\sum_{i\le m}\lambda_i(A)=\min\{\operatorname{tr}V^*AV:V^*V=I_m\}$ and the top-$m$ sum is the corresponding maximum, attained at eigenvectors.
items.note: Existing atlas candidate (cites this label).

items.label: Def 4.3.41
items.name: Majorization
items.statement: $x\in\mathbb R^n$ majorizes $y$ if every partial sum of the $k$ largest entries of $x$ dominates that of $y$, with equality of total sums.

items.label: Def 4.3.43
items.statement: The nonincreasing and nondecreasing rearrangements $z^\downarrow$, $z^\uparrow$ of a real vector.
items.note: Mathlib has sorting of finite lists/tuples (`Tuple.sort`) but not the vector rearrangement API used here.

items.label: Thm 4.3.45
items.name: Schur's majorization theorem
items.statement: Schur: the eigenvalue vector of a Hermitian matrix majorizes its diagonal; equality at step $k<n$ forces a permutation-similar direct sum.

items.label: Thm 4.3.47
items.name: Fan and Lidskii majorization
items.statement: For Hermitian $A,B$: (Fan) $\lambda^\downarrow(A)+\lambda^\downarrow(B)$ majorizes $\lambda(A+B)$; (Lidskii) $\lambda(A+B)$ majorizes $\lambda^\downarrow(A)+\lambda^\uparrow(B)$.

items.label: Thm 4.3.48
items.name: Horn converse to Schur
items.statement: Horn: if $x$ majorizes $y$ there is a real orthogonal $Q$ with $\operatorname{diag}(Q^T\operatorname{diag}(x)Q)=y$.

items.label: Thm 4.3.49
items.name: Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya / Rado
items.statement: TFAE: $x$ majorizes $y$; $y=Sx$ for a doubly stochastic $S$; $y$ is a convex combination of permutations of $x$.
items.note: Birkhoff step is Mathlib `doublyStochastic_eq_convexHull_permMatrix`.

items.label: Thm 4.3.50
items.statement: $x$ majorizes $\operatorname{Re}z$ iff some $A$ has eigenvalues $z_i$ while its Hermitian part $(A+A^*)/2$ has eigenvalues $x_i$.
items.note: Candidate `real-part-eigenvalue-majorization` (later).

items.label: Lem 4.3.51
items.statement: If $x$ majorizes $y$ then $\sum w_i^\downarrow x_i^\uparrow\le\sum w_i^\downarrow y_i\le\sum w_i^\downarrow x_i^\downarrow$, with equality conditions via partial sums.
items.note: Rearrangement-type characterisation; fold into the majorization entry.

items.label: Thm 4.3.53
items.name: Eigenvalue trace inequality
items.statement: For Hermitian $A,B$: $\sum\lambda_i^\downarrow(A)\lambda_i^\uparrow(B)\le\operatorname{tr}AB\le\sum\lambda_i^\downarrow(A)\lambda_i^\downarrow(B)$; equality forces commuting and simultaneous ordered diagonalisation.
items.note: Existing candidate states the upper bound; NLAlib has the singular-value (von Neumann) analogue and the overlap identity `re_trace_pow_mul_pow_eq_sum_overlap`, not this eigenvalue form.

items.label: Lem 4.4.2
items.statement: For an eigenpair of $A\bar A$, the span of $A\bar x$ and $x$ yields a coneigenvector of $A$ (dimension-one and dimension-two cases).
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.4.3
items.statement: If $A\bar A$ has $p$ real nonnegative eigenvalues, $A$ is unitarily congruent to a block upper triangular form with $p$ leading $1\times1$ blocks.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.4.4
items.statement: Unitary-congruence triangularization exists iff all eigenvalues of $A\bar A$ are nonnegative; refinement with $n-1$ such eigenvalues.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Prop 4.4.5
items.statement: Canonical form of a $2\times2$ matrix under unitary congruence in terms of the singular values of its symmetric part.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.4.9
items.statement: Youla: every $A$ is unitarily congruent to a block triangular form with $1\times1$ and $2\times2$ diagonal blocks determined by the eigenvalues of $A\bar A$.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.4.13
items.statement: Non-real eigenvalues of $A\bar A$ occur in conjugate pairs and negative real ones in equal pairs.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 4.4.14
items.statement: $A$ is conjugate normal if $AA^*=\overline{A^*A}$.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Lem 4.4.15
items.statement: A block upper triangular matrix is conjugate normal iff it is block diagonal with conjugate-normal blocks.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.4.16
items.statement: Conjugate normal matrices are exactly those unitarily congruent to a direct sum of $2\times2$ real blocks and nonnegative scalars.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.4.18
items.statement: A matrix is conjugate normal iff it is unitarily congruent to a direct sum of nonnegative multiples of real orthogonal matrices.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.4.19
items.statement: A skew-symmetric matrix has even rank, paired singular values, and a canonical unitary-congruence form.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.4.21
items.statement: Every unitary matrix is unitarily congruent to $I\oplus$ a direct sum of $2\times2$ real rotation-type blocks.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.4.24
items.statement: Every complex square matrix is similar to a complex symmetric matrix.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.4.25
items.statement: Every $A$ is a product of two complex symmetric matrices, one of which can be nonsingular.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Lem 4.4.26
items.statement: $X^TX$ is nonsingular iff $X=YB$ with $Y^TY=I$ (complex orthogonal columns) and $B$ nonsingular.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.4.27
items.statement: A complex symmetric matrix is diagonalizable iff it is complex orthogonally diagonalizable.
items.note: Unitary congruence / complex-symmetric (coneigenvalue) theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 4.5.4
items.statement: $B$ is *congruent to $A$ if $B=SAS^*$ and congruent if $B=SAS^T$ for some nonsingular $S$.
items.note: Real case as equivalence of quadratic forms; NLAlib bridges it in `equivalent_toQuadraticForm'_transpose_mul_mul`.

items.label: Thm 4.5.5
items.statement: *Congruence and congruence are equivalence relations.

items.label: Def 4.5.6
items.statement: The inertia of a Hermitian matrix is the triple of counts of positive, negative and zero eigenvalues; the inertia matrix is the corresponding signature diagonal.
items.note: Real symmetric; Mathlib also has `QuadraticMap.sigPos`/`sigNeg`.

items.label: Thm 4.5.7
items.statement: Every Hermitian matrix is *congruent to its inertia matrix.
items.note: Real quadratic forms.

items.label: Thm 4.5.8
items.name: Sylvester's law of inertia
items.statement: Sylvester's law of inertia: Hermitian $A,B$ are *congruent iff they have the same numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues.
items.note: NLAlib states the invariance direction (real symmetric); the converse follows from Mathlib Thm 4.5.7 but is not stated as an iff.

items.label: Thm 4.5.9
items.name: Ostrowski's theorem
items.statement: Ostrowski: for Hermitian $A$ and nonsingular $S$, $\lambda_k(SAS^*)=\theta_k\lambda_k(A)$ with $\theta_k\in[\sigma_n(S)^2,\sigma_1(S)^2]$.
items.note: Candidate `ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues`.

items.label: Cor 4.5.11
items.statement: The same multiplicative eigenvalue bounds hold for singular $S$ (with $\theta_k\ge0$); $SAS^*$ has at most as many positive (negative) eigenvalues as $A$.
items.note: Candidate `ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues`.

items.label: Thm 4.5.12
items.statement: Complex symmetric $A,B$ are congruent ($A=SBS^T$) iff they have the same rank.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.13
items.statement: Under congruence $A\mapsto SAS^T$ of a complex symmetric matrix, its Takagi values scale by factors in $[\lambda_1(SS^*),\lambda_n(SS^*)]$.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.15
items.statement: (a) Hermitian $A,B$ are simultaneously unitarily diagonalizable iff $AB=BA$; (b) analogous criteria for complex symmetric pairs via normality of $A\bar B$.
items.note: (a) as commuting symmetric operators in Mathlib; (b) complex-symmetric part out of scope.

items.label: Def 4.5.16
items.statement: $A$ is condiagonalizable if $A=S\Lambda\bar S^{-1}$ for nonsingular $S$ and diagonal $\Lambda$.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.17
items.statement: (a) For Hermitian $A$ nonsingular and $B$ Hermitian, $A=S\Lambda S^*$, $B=SMS^*$ with real diagonal $\Lambda,M$ iff $A^{-1}B$ is diagonalizable with real eigenvalues; (b) complex symmetric analogue.
items.note: Part (a) belongs to candidate `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence`; part (b) out of scope.

items.label: Lem 4.5.18
items.statement: $A=H+iK$ is diagonalizable by *congruence iff $H$ and $K$ are simultaneously diagonalizable by *congruence.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.21
items.statement: Canonical form for *congruence: every square matrix is *congruent to a unique direct sum of nilpotent Jordan blocks, unimodular-scaled blocks and $H_{2k}(\mu)$ blocks.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.22
items.statement: Cancellation for *congruence: $A\oplus C$ and $B\oplus C$ are *congruent iff $A$ and $B$ are.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.24
items.statement: TFAE for diagonalizability of $A=H+iK$ by *congruence in terms of its regular part and the cosquare.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.25
items.statement: Canonical form for congruence: unique direct sum of nilpotent Jordan blocks, $\Gamma_k$ blocks and $H_{2k}(\mu)$ blocks.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.26
items.statement: Cancellation for congruence: $A\oplus C$ and $B\oplus C$ are congruent iff $A$ and $B$ are.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.5.27
items.statement: Nonsingular $A,B$ are congruent iff their cosquares $A^{-T}A$ and $B^{-T}B$ are similar.
items.note: Congruence (T-congruence) and *congruence canonical-form theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Ex 4.5.P21
items.name: Haynsworth's inertia additivity
items.statement: Haynsworth: if $A=\begin{bmatrix}B&C\\C^*&D\end{bmatrix}$ is Hermitian with $B$ nonsingular and $S=D-C^*B^{-1}C$, then $i_\pm(A)=i_\pm(B)+i_\pm(S)$ and $i_0(A)=i_0(S)$.
items.note: Candidate `haynsworth-inertia-additivity`; NLAlib has the scalar-pivot special cases (`posDef_iff_pivotSchur`, `card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_neg_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul`).

items.label: Def 4.6.1
items.statement: $A$ and $B$ are consimilar if $A=SB\bar S^{-1}$ for a nonsingular $S$.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 4.6.2
items.statement: Contriangularizable, block contriangularizable and condiagonalizable matrices via $S^{-1}A\bar S$.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.6.3
items.statement: A matrix is contriangularizable iff it is unitarily contriangularizable iff $A\bar A$ has only real nonnegative eigenvalues.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.6.4
items.statement: A matrix is unitarily condiagonalizable iff it is complex symmetric.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 4.6.5
items.statement: Coneigenvectors and coneigenvalues: $A\bar x=\lambda x$ with $x\ne0$.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Prop 4.6.6
items.statement: If $\lambda\ge0$ is an eigenvalue of $A\bar A$ then $\sqrt\lambda$ is a coneigenvalue of $A$.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Prop 4.6.7
items.statement: Coneigenvectors for coneigenvalues of distinct moduli are linearly independent.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.6.8
items.statement: If $A\bar A$ has $k$ distinct nonnegative eigenvalues then $A$ has $k$ independent coneigenvectors.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Lem 4.6.9
items.statement: $A\bar A=I$ iff $A=S\bar S^{-1}$ for a nonsingular $S$.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.6.11
items.statement: $A$ is condiagonalizable iff $A\bar A$ is diagonalizable with nonnegative eigenvalues and $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}A\bar A$.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.6.12
items.statement: Canonical form for consimilarity as a unique direct sum of three block types.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.6.13
items.statement: Cancellation for consimilarity.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.6.14
items.statement: $A,B$ are consimilar iff $A\bar A\sim B\bar B$ and certain alternating-product ranks agree.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.6.15
items.statement: Every $A$ is consimilar to $-A$, $\bar A$, $A^T$, $A^*$, to a Hermitian matrix and to a real matrix.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.6.16
items.statement: $A\bar A$ is similar to the square of a real matrix.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 4.6.17
items.statement: Factorizations $A=HS$ with $H$ Hermitian, $S$ symmetric, and related consequences of the consimilarity canonical form.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 4.6.18
items.statement: TFAE characterisations of consimilarity via a real-representation block matrix.
items.note: Consimilarity / coneigenvalue theory over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 5.1.1
items.statement: A (vector) norm on a real or complex vector space is a nonnegative, positive, absolutely homogeneous function obeying the triangle inequality; a seminorm drops positivity.

items.label: Lem 5.1.2
items.statement: For a seminorm, $|\,\|x\|-\|y\|\,|\le\|x-y\|$.

items.label: Def 5.1.3
items.statement: An inner product is a positive, additive, homogeneous, Hermitian-symmetric form on $V\times V$.

items.label: Thm 5.1.4
items.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
items.statement: Cauchy–Schwarz: $|\langle x,y\rangle|^2\le\langle x,x\rangle\langle y,y\rangle$, with equality iff $x,y$ are linearly dependent.

items.label: Cor 5.1.7
items.statement: An inner product induces a norm $\|x\|=\langle x,x\rangle^{1/2}$.

items.label: Thm 5.1.8
items.statement: A semi-inner product satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz and induces a seminorm.

items.label: Thm 5.3.1
