items.statement: If $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb R^m$ is monotone on the nonnegative orthant and $\|\cdot\|_{\alpha_i}$ are norms, then $x\mapsto\|[\|x\|_{\alpha_1},\dots,\|x\|_{\alpha_m}]\|$ is a norm.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Def 5.4.1
items.statement: A sequence converges to $x$ in a norm if $\|x^{(k)}-x\|\to0$.
items.note: Convergence in the norm topology.

items.label: Lem 5.4.3
items.statement: For fixed vectors $x^{(i)}$, $z\mapsto\|\sum z_ix^{(i)}\|$ is uniformly continuous on $\mathbb F^m$.

items.label: Thm 5.4.4
items.statement: Two positive, homogeneous, continuous functions on a finite-dimensional space are equivalent: $C_mf_1\le f_2\le C_Mf_1$.
items.note: Mathlib states it for norms (continuity of linear maps in finite dimension); the pre-norm generality is not stated.

items.label: Cor 5.4.5
items.statement: Any two norms on a finite-dimensional real or complex space are equivalent with explicit constants $C_m,C_M>0$.

items.label: Cor 5.4.6
items.statement: In finite dimension, convergence in one norm is equivalent to convergence in any other norm.

items.label: Def 5.4.7
items.statement: Two norms are equivalent if they have the same convergent sequences.

items.label: Cor 5.4.8
items.statement: The unit ball and unit sphere of a (pre-)norm on $\mathbb F^n$ are compact.

items.label: Def 5.4.9
items.statement: Cauchy sequence with respect to a norm.

items.label: Thm 5.4.10
items.statement: In a finite-dimensional normed space a sequence converges iff it is Cauchy.

items.label: Def 5.4.11
items.statement: A normed space is complete if every Cauchy sequence converges.

items.label: Def 5.4.12
items.statement: The dual norm of a pre-norm $f$ is $f^D(y)=\max_{f(x)=1}\operatorname{Re}y^*x$.
items.note: Mathlib has the dual of a normed space with the operator norm; the pre-norm generality is out of scope.

items.label: Lem 5.4.13
items.statement: Duality inequalities $|y^*x|\le f(x)f^D(y)$ and $|y^*x|\le f^D(x)f(y)$.

items.label: Lem 5.4.16
items.statement: Dual of $cf$ is $c^{-1}f^D$, and $f\le g$ implies $f^D\ge g^D$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.4.17
items.statement: A norm equals a multiple of its own dual, $\|x\|=c\|x\|^D$, iff it is $\sqrt c$ times the Euclidean norm; the Euclidean norm is the unique self-dual norm.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Def 5.4.18
items.statement: A norm on $\mathbb F^n$ is monotone if $|x|\le|y|$ entrywise implies $\|x\|\le\|y\|$, and absolute if $\|x\|=\||x|\|$.
items.note: Needed to define symmetric gauge functions (Def 7.4.7.1); fold into the existing candidate.

items.label: Thm 5.4.19
items.statement: For absolute norms, the dual is $\max_x|y|^T|x|/\|x\|$ and is itself absolute and monotone.
items.note: Low priority; supports the gauge-function theory.

items.label: Def 5.5.1
items.statement: Closed ball of radius $r$ about $x$, and the unit ball of a norm.

items.label: Def 5.5.2
items.statement: A norm is polyhedral if its unit ball is a polyhedron.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Def 5.5.3
items.statement: Interior points, open and closed sets, limit points, closure, boundary and boundedness relative to a norm.

items.label: Obs 5.5.4
items.statement: In positive dimension, $0$ is an interior point of the unit ball.

items.label: Obs 5.5.5
items.statement: The unit ball is equilibrated (balanced): $x$ in the ball implies $\alpha x$ is, for $|\alpha|=1$.

items.label: Obs 5.5.6
items.statement: The unit ball of a norm on a finite-dimensional space is compact.

items.label: Obs 5.5.7
items.statement: The unit ball of a norm is convex.

items.label: Thm 5.5.8
items.statement: A set in a finite-dimensional space is the unit ball of a norm iff it is compact, convex, equilibrated and has $0$ as an interior point.
items.note: Mathlib has the Minkowski gauge of a balanced convex absorbent set; the exact iff is not packaged.

items.label: Thm 5.5.9
items.name: Duality theorem
items.statement: Duality theorem: $f^{DD}\le f$, the $f^{DD}$-ball is the closed convex hull of the $f$-ball, and $f^{DD}=f$ when $f$ is a norm.
items.note: Norm case (isometric bidual embedding) in Mathlib; pre-norm convex-hull part not stated.

items.label: Cor 5.5.11
items.statement: An absolute norm on $\mathbb R^n$ or $\mathbb C^n$ is monotone.
items.note: Used to show a unitarily invariant norm is monotone on diagonal matrices (argument after Thm 7.4.9.1).

items.label: Def 5.6.1
items.statement: The matrix norm induced by a vector norm: $|||A|||=\max_{\|x\|=1}\|Ax\|$.
items.note: NLAlib defines the spectral (ℓ2-induced) case as `NLAlib.specNorm`.

items.label: Thm 5.6.2
items.statement: An induced norm has $|||I|||=1$, $\|Ay\|\le|||A|||\|y\|$, is submultiplicative, and $|||A|||=\max_{\|x\|=\|y\|^D=1}|y^*Ax|$.
items.note: NLAlib proves the spectral-norm instances (`specNorm_mul_le`, `sqrt_mulVec_dotProduct_le_specNorm_mul`).

items.label: Def 5.6.3
items.statement: The induced (operator, lub) norm; unital norms and compatibility of a vector norm with a matrix norm.

items.label: Thm 5.6.7
items.statement: $A\mapsto|||SAS^{-1}|||$ is a matrix norm, induced by $\|S^{-1}\cdot\|$ when $|||\cdot|||$ is induced.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.9
items.statement: For any matrix norm and eigenvalue $\lambda$: $|\lambda|\le\rho(A)\le|||A|||$, and $\rho(A)\ge|\lambda|\ge1/|||A^{-1}|||$ for nonsingular $A$.
items.note: Banach-algebra statement; applies to any submultiplicative unital matrix norm.

items.label: Lem 5.6.10
items.statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a matrix norm with $\rho(A)\le|||A|||\le\rho(A)+\varepsilon$.
items.note: Candidate `spectral-radius-power-convergence`.

items.label: Lem 5.6.11
items.statement: If some matrix norm has $|||A|||<1$ then $A^k\to0$.
items.note: Candidate `spectral-radius-power-convergence`; Mathlib has `tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_norm_lt_one` for the norm itself.

items.label: Thm 5.6.12
items.statement: $A^k\to0$ iff $\rho(A)<1$.
items.note: Candidate `spectral-radius-power-convergence`; same statement as hj13-part1 candidate `matrix-power-convergence` (Thm 3.2.5.2), to be merged.

items.label: Cor 5.6.13
items.statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C$ with $|(A^k)_{ij}|\le C(\rho(A)+\varepsilon)^k$ for all $k$.
items.note: Candidate `spectral-radius-power-convergence`; also stated in hj13-part1 candidate `matrix-power-convergence`, to be merged.

items.label: Cor 5.6.14
items.name: Gelfand's formula
items.statement: Gelfand: $\rho(A)=\lim_k|||A^k|||^{1/k}$ for every matrix norm.

items.label: Thm 5.6.15
items.statement: A matrix power series $\sum a_kA^k$ converges if $\rho(A)$ is below the scalar radius of convergence (in particular if some matrix norm of $A$ is).
items.note: Candidate `spectral-radius-power-convergence`; Mathlib has the norm-based version through `FormalMultilinearSeries` radius.

items.label: Cor 5.6.16
items.name: Neumann series
items.statement: If $|||I-A|||<1$ for some matrix norm then $A$ is nonsingular and $A^{-1}=\sum_k(I-A)^k$.
items.note: Mathlib states it for any complete normed ring; NLAlib states the spectral-norm case with explicit constants.

items.label: Cor 5.6.17
items.name: Lévy–Desplanques theorem
items.statement: A strictly diagonally dominant matrix is nonsingular.

items.label: Thm 5.6.18
items.statement: For induced norms $|||\cdot|||_\alpha,|||\cdot|||_\beta$, $\max_A|||A|||_\alpha/|||A|||_\beta=R_{\alpha\beta}R_{\beta\alpha}$ with $R$ the vector-norm comparison constants.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Lem 5.6.23
items.statement: $R_{\alpha\beta}R_{\beta\alpha}\ge1$ with equality iff the two vector norms are proportional iff the induced norms coincide.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Cor 5.6.25
items.statement: If one induced norm is dominated by another, they are equal.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.26
items.statement: For a matrix norm and nonzero $z$, $\|x\|_z=|||xz^*|||$ is a vector norm whose induced norm is dominated by the given matrix norm.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Def 5.6.31
items.statement: A matrix norm is minimal if no other matrix norm lies below it.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.32
items.statement: A matrix norm is induced iff it is minimal iff it equals $N_z$ for all (some) $z\ne0$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.33
items.statement: Characterisation of when the norms $\|\cdot\|_z$ are all proportional, and consequences for induced norms.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.34
items.statement: For a unitarily invariant matrix norm: $\|\cdot\|_z$ is a multiple of the Euclidean norm, $N_z$ is the spectral norm, $|||A|||_2\le|||A|||$, and an induced unitarily invariant norm is the spectral norm.
items.note: Part (d) (spectral norm is the least unitarily invariant matrix norm) pairs with Thm 7.4.10.1.

items.label: Thm 5.6.35
items.statement: The norm induced by $\|\cdot\|$ also arises from the dual norm (via $A^*$); a self-adjoint induced norm is the spectral norm.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.36
items.statement: For an induced norm, TFAE: the vector norm is absolute; it is monotone; diagonal matrices have norm $\max|\lambda_i|$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Def 5.6.38
items.statement: Dual of a norm on $M_n$: $\|A\|^D=\max_{\|B\|=1}\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}B^*A$.
items.note: Needed for nuclear/spectral duality; fold into the Ky Fan norms entry.

items.label: Thm 5.6.39
items.statement: A norm on $M_n$ is self-adjoint (unitarily invariant) iff its dual is.
items.note: Low priority remark.

items.label: Thm 5.6.40
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.41
items.statement: For an induced norm: $|||A^*|||$ is a max over rank-one $B$, $|||A^*|||\le|||A|||^D$, the dual is a matrix norm, with equality for rank $\le1$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.6.42
items.statement: If an absolute norm induces $|||\cdot|||$ then $|||\cdot|||^D$ is a matrix norm and $|||\Lambda|||^D=\sum|\lambda_i|$ on diagonals (so the dual of the spectral norm is the trace norm).
items.note: Only the spectral/trace-norm duality is wanted (already in the Ky Fan norms entry).

items.label: Thm 5.7.8
items.statement: Any pre-norm $f$ on $M_n$ is equivalent to any matrix norm: $C_m|||A|||\le f(A)\le C_M|||A|||$.
items.note: Norm case via finite-dimensional norm equivalence; pre-norm generality not stated.

items.label: Thm 5.7.10
items.statement: For any pre-norm (in particular any vector norm) on $M_n$, $f(A^k)^{1/k}\to\rho(A)$.
items.note: Follows from Gelfand plus norm equivalence; not stated for non-submultiplicative norms.

items.label: Thm 5.7.11
items.statement: For a vector norm $G$ on $M_n$, $\gamma G$ is a matrix norm iff $\gamma\ge c(G)=\max_{G(A)=G(B)=1}G(AB)$, with bounds on $c(G)$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Def 5.7.12
items.statement: A vector norm on $\mathbb C^n$ and a norm $G$ on $M_n$ are compatible if $\|Ax\|\le G(A)\|x\|$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.7.13
items.statement: Every matrix norm has a compatible vector norm and every vector norm has a compatible matrix norm.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.7.14
items.statement: A norm on $M_n$ compatible with a vector norm satisfies $G(A_1)\cdots G(A_k)\ge\rho(A_1\cdots A_k)$; in particular it is spectrally dominant.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Lem 5.7.16
items.statement: A norm satisfying (5.7.15) dominates a multiple of the spectral norm of products.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.7.17
items.statement: A norm on $M_n$ is compatible with some vector norm iff it satisfies (5.7.15).
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.7.18
items.statement: Every vector norm is compatible with some norm on $M_n$ that is not a matrix norm.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Lem 5.7.19
items.statement: For a spectrally dominant norm, a non-semisimple dominant eigenvalue forces $G(A)>\rho(A)$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.label: Thm 5.7.20
items.statement: A norm on $M_n$ is spectrally dominant iff $G(A^k)\le\gamma_AG(A)^k$ for all $k$.
items.note: General (pre-)norm / induced-norm theory; NLAlib works with Euclidean, Frobenius, spectral and unitarily invariant norms, and Mathlib covers the operator-norm basics.

items.name: Condition numbers: inverses and linear systems
items.statement: Condition numbers: if $|||A^{-1}\Delta A|||<1$ then $A+\Delta A$ is invertible with relative inverse error at most $\kappa(A)\frac{|||\Delta A|||/|||A|||}{1-\kappa(A)|||\Delta A|||/|||A|||}$; analogous forward and a-posteriori error bounds for $Ax=b$.
items.note: Unnumbered section (no numbered statements); NLAlib proves the spectral-norm versions.

items.label: Thm 6.1.1
items.name: Geršgorin disc theorem
items.statement: Geršgorin: every eigenvalue lies in $\bigcup_i\{z:|z-a_{ii}|\le R_i\}$, $R_i$ the deleted row sums; a union of $k$ discs disjoint from the others contains exactly $k$ eigenvalues.
items.note: Mathlib has the inclusion part; the counting part for isolated unions of discs is missing (candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`).

items.label: Cor 6.1.3
items.statement: The same holds with deleted column sums $C_j$ (discs of $A^T$), including the counting statement.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. Inclusion part is Mathlib `eigenvalue_mem_ball` applied to $A^T$.

items.label: Cor 6.1.5
items.statement: $\rho(A)\le\min\{\max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|,\max_j\sum_i|a_{ij}|\}$.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. Follows from Mathlib `spectralRadius_le_nnnorm` with `Matrix.linfty_opNorm_def`, not stated.

items.label: Cor 6.1.6
items.statement: Scaled Geršgorin: for positive $p_i$ the eigenvalues lie in the discs of $D^{-1}AD$, radii $p_i^{-1}\sum_{j\ne i}p_j|a_{ij}|$.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`.

items.label: Cor 6.1.8
items.statement: $\rho(A)\le\min_{p>0}\max_i p_i^{-1}\sum_jp_j|a_{ij}|$ and the column analogue.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`.

items.label: Def 6.1.9
items.statement: $A$ is (strictly) diagonally dominant if $|a_{ii}|\ge R_i$ ($>R_i$) for every row.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`.

items.label: Thm 6.1.10
items.statement: A strictly diagonally dominant matrix is nonsingular; with positive diagonal all eigenvalues have positive real part; if also Hermitian it is positive definite.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. Part (a) is in Mathlib; (b) and (c) are missing.

items.label: Thm 6.1.11
items.statement: A diagonally dominant matrix with nonzero diagonal and strict dominance in at least $n-1$ rows is nonsingular.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. (later)

items.label: Lem 6.2.2
items.statement: $\lambda$ avoids the interiors of all Geršgorin discs iff $|\lambda-a_{ii}|\ge R_i$ for all $i$; characterisation of boundary points of the Geršgorin set.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Lem 6.2.3
items.statement: If an eigenvalue satisfies (6.2.2a), every row where the eigenvector peaks in modulus has its Geršgorin circle through $\lambda$, and the peak propagates along nonzero entries.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Thm 6.2.5
items.statement: If all entries are nonzero and an eigenvalue satisfies (6.2.2a), every Geršgorin circle passes through it and the eigenvector has constant modulus.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Cor 6.2.6
items.statement: A diagonally dominant matrix with all entries nonzero and one strictly dominant row is nonsingular.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Def 6.2.7
items.statement: Property SC: every ordered pair of indices is joined by a chain of nonzero entries.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Thm 6.2.8
items.statement: With property SC, an eigenvalue satisfying (6.2.2a) lies on every Geršgorin circle and its eigenvector has constant modulus.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Cor 6.2.9
items.statement: A diagonally dominant matrix with property SC and one strictly dominant row is nonsingular.
items.note: Boundary-eigenvalue / property-SC machinery behind Taussky's theorem; only the resulting criteria (Thm 6.2.26, Cor 6.2.27) are candidates.

items.label: Def 6.2.10
items.statement: Entrywise absolute value $|A|$ and the 0/1 indicator matrix $M(A)$.
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Def 6.2.11
items.statement: The directed graph $\Gamma(A)$ with an arc $P_i\to P_j$ iff $a_{ij}\ne0$.
items.note: Mathlib builds the quiver of a matrix for `Matrix.IsIrreducible`.

items.label: Def 6.2.12
items.statement: Directed paths, their lengths and cycles in a directed graph.

items.label: Def 6.2.13
items.statement: A directed graph is strongly connected if every ordered pair of distinct nodes is joined by a directed path.
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Thm 6.2.14
items.statement: $A$ has property SC iff $\Gamma(A)$ is strongly connected.
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Obs 6.2.15
items.statement: If two nodes are joined by a directed path, they are joined by one of length at most $n-1$.
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Thm 6.2.16
items.statement: There is a directed path of length $m$ from $P_i$ to $P_j$ iff $(|A|^m)_{ij}\ne0$ iff $(M(A)^m)_{ij}\ne0$.
items.note: Mathlib states it for nonnegative matrices.

items.label: Def 6.2.17
items.statement: Entrywise nonnegative ($A\ge0$) and positive ($A>0$) matrices.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius notation; Mathlib uses `0 ≤ A` entrywise via `Pi` order where needed.

items.label: Cor 6.2.18
items.statement: $|A|^m>0$ iff every node reaches every node by a directed path of length exactly $m$.
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Cor 6.2.19
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Cor 6.2.20
items.statement: For $i\ne j$, $P_i$ reaches $P_j$ iff $((I+|A|)^{n-1})_{ij}\ne0$.
items.note: Directed-graph bookkeeping for irreducibility (combinatorial); Mathlib has `Matrix.IsIrreducible` for the parts NLAlib could need.

items.label: Def 6.2.21
items.statement: $A$ is reducible if a permutation similarity brings it to block upper triangular form with square diagonal blocks.
items.note: Mathlib defines irreducibility (for nonnegative matrices) via strong connectivity of the quiver.

items.label: Def 6.2.22
items.statement: $A$ is irreducible if it is not reducible.

items.label: Thm 6.2.23
items.statement: TFAE: $A$ irreducible; $(I+|A|)^{n-1}>0$; $(I+M(A))^{n-1}>0$.
items.note: Mathlib states the power-positivity criterion for nonnegative matrices; the block-reducibility form is not stated.

items.label: Thm 6.2.24
items.statement: TFAE: irreducible; $(I+|A|)^{n-1}>0$; $(I+M(A))^{n-1}>0$; $\Gamma(A)$ strongly connected.

items.label: Def 6.2.25
items.statement: $A$ is irreducibly diagonally dominant if irreducible, diagonally dominant, and strictly dominant in some row.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. (later)

items.label: Thm 6.2.26
items.name: Taussky's theorem
items.statement: Taussky: for irreducible $A$, an eigenvalue satisfying (6.2.2a) lies on every Geršgorin circle.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. (later)

items.label: Cor 6.2.27
items.name: Taussky
items.statement: An irreducibly diagonally dominant matrix is nonsingular, and with positive diagonal all eigenvalues have positive real part.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`. (later)

items.label: Obs 6.3.1
items.statement: For diagonalizable $A=S\Lambda S^{-1}$, every eigenvalue of $A+E$ is within $\kappa_\infty(S)|||E|||_\infty$ of an eigenvalue of $A$.
items.note: Candidate `bauer-fike`.

items.label: Thm 6.3.2
items.name: Bauer–Fike theorem
items.statement: Bauer–Fike: for diagonalizable $A=S\Lambda S^{-1}$ and a norm induced by an absolute vector norm, each eigenvalue of $A+E$ is within $\kappa(S)|||E|||$ of an eigenvalue of $A$.
items.note: Candidate `bauer-fike`.

items.label: Cor 6.3.4
items.statement: If $A$ is normal, every eigenvalue of $A+E$ is within $\|E\|_2$ of an eigenvalue of $A$.
items.note: Candidate `bauer-fike`.

items.label: Thm 6.3.5
items.name: Hoffman–Wielandt theorem
items.statement: Hoffman–Wielandt: for normal $A$ and $A+E$ there is a matching permutation with $\sum_i|\hat\lambda_{\sigma(i)}-\lambda_i|^2\le\|E\|_F^2$.
items.note: Normal-matrix form: candidate `hoffman-wielandt-normal`; the symmetric form is the existing atlas candidate.

items.label: Cor 6.3.8
items.statement: For Hermitian $A$ and normal $A+E$, with eigenvalues ordered increasingly (by real part), $\sum_i|\hat\lambda_i-\lambda_i|^2\le\|E\|_F^2$.
items.note: Existing atlas candidate (cites this label). NLAlib has the singular-value analogue `sum_sq_singularValues_add_sub_le_frobSq`.

items.label: Lem 6.3.10
items.statement: For a simple eigenvalue with right/left eigenvectors $x,y$: $y^*x\ne0$, and $A$ is similar to $\lambda\oplus A_1$ with $\lambda\notin\sigma(A_1)$ via $S=[x\ S_1]$.
items.note: Candidate `simple-eigenvalue-perturbation` (later).

items.label: Thm 6.3.12
items.statement: A simple eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ extends to a continuous, differentiable eigenvalue $\lambda(t)$ of $A+tE$ with $\lambda'(0)=y^*Ex/y^*x$.
items.note: Candidate `simple-eigenvalue-perturbation` (later).

items.label: Thm 6.3.14
items.statement: Residual bounds: for diagonalizable $A$ and any $\hat x\ne0,\hat\lambda$, some eigenvalue satisfies $|\hat\lambda-\lambda|\le\kappa(S)\|r\|/\|\hat x\|$; for normal $A$, $|\hat\lambda-\lambda|\le\|r\|_2/\|\hat x\|_2$.
items.note: Normal case extends the existing symmetric candidate; the diagonalizable case goes in candidate `bauer-fike`.

items.label: Thm 6.4.1
items.statement: Ostrowski: for $\alpha\in[0,1]$ the eigenvalues lie in $\bigcup_i\{z:|z-a_{ii}|\le R_i^\alpha C_i^{1-\alpha}\}$.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 6.4.7
items.statement: Brauer: for $n\ge2$ the eigenvalues lie in the union of the ovals of Cassini $|z-a_{ii}||z-a_{jj}|\le R_iR_j$.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 6.4.11
items.statement: Nonsingularity from $|a_{ii}|>R_i^\alpha C_i^{1-\alpha}$ for all $i$ (Ostrowski) or $|a_{ii}a_{jj}|>R_iR_j$ for all $i\ne j$ (Brauer).
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Lem 6.4.16
items.statement: Weak irreducibility is characterised by off-diagonal entry pairs of $(I+|A|)^{n-1}$.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Lem 6.4.17
items.statement: A preorder on a finite nonempty set has a maximal element.
items.note: Order-theoretic helper for Brualdi's theorem.

items.label: Thm 6.4.18
items.statement: Brualdi: for weakly irreducible $A$, eigenvalues lie in the union over cycles $\gamma$ of $\{z:\prod_{i\in\gamma}|z-a_{ii}|\le\prod_{i\in\gamma}R_i\}$.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 6.4.26
items.statement: Brualdi: for irreducible $A$, a boundary point of the cycle set is an eigenvalue only if it lies on the boundary of every cycle set.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Cor 6.4.29
items.statement: Cycle-wise diagonal dominance conditions guaranteeing nonsingularity.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 6.4.30
items.statement: Kolotilina: for irreducible $A$ the eigenvalues lie in Cassini ovals restricted to pairs with $|a_{ij}|+|a_{ji}|\ne0$.
items.note: Refined eigenvalue inclusion regions (Ostrowski/Brauer ovals, Brualdi cycle sets); no randomized-NLA consumer.

items.label: Obs 7.1.2
items.statement: Principal submatrices of a positive definite (semidefinite) matrix are positive definite (semidefinite).

items.label: Obs 7.1.3
items.statement: Nonnegative combinations of PSD matrices are PSD, and PD if some PD term has a positive coefficient.

items.label: Obs 7.1.4
items.statement: Eigenvalues of a PD (PSD) matrix are positive (nonnegative).

items.label: Cor 7.1.5
items.statement: For PSD (PD) $A$, $\operatorname{tr}A$, $\det A$ and all principal minors are nonnegative (positive); $\operatorname{tr}A=0$ iff $A=0$.

items.label: Obs 7.1.6
items.statement: For PSD $A$, $x^*Ax=0$ iff $Ax=0$.

items.label: Cor 7.1.7
items.statement: A PSD matrix is PD iff it is nonsingular.

items.label: Obs 7.1.8
items.statement: For PSD $A$, $C^*AC$ is PSD with $\ker C^*AC=\ker AC$ and equal ranks; for PD $A$, $\operatorname{rank}C^*AC=\operatorname{rank}C$ and $C^*AC\succ0$ iff $C$ has full column rank.
items.note: PSD/PD transfer in Mathlib; the null-space and rank identities for general PSD $A$ are only stated for $A=I$.

items.label: Obs 7.1.9
items.statement: A Hermitian matrix is PSD iff it is a limit of PD matrices.
items.note: Closedness of the PSD cone (the "if" direction) is in NLAlib; the approximation $A+\varepsilon I$ direction is not stated.

items.label: Obs 7.1.10
items.statement: PSD matrices have the row and column inclusion property; a zero diagonal entry forces its whole row and column to vanish.
items.note: Zero-diagonal case proved (real and complex); the block inclusion $(I-AA^\dagger)B=0$ is inside `posSemidef_fromBlocks_iff`, which is currently assumed (sorry).

items.label: Lem 7.1.11
items.statement: If $H(A)=(A+A^*)/2\succeq0$ then $\ker A\subseteq\ker H(A)$, $\operatorname{rank}H(A)\le\operatorname{rank}A$, and equality of null spaces is equivalent to equality of ranks.
items.note: Candidate `psd-hermitian-part` (later).

items.label: Obs 7.1.12
items.statement: If $H(A)\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}H(A)$ then $A$ has the row and column inclusion properties.
items.note: Candidate `psd-hermitian-part` (later).

items.label: Cor 7.1.13
items.statement: If $H(A)\succ0$ then $A$ has the row and column inclusion properties.
items.note: Candidate `psd-hermitian-part` (later).

items.label: Obs 7.1.14
items.statement: For PSD $A,B$: $A+B=0$ iff $A=B=0$, and $\operatorname{rank}(A+B)>0$ iff one of them is nonzero.
items.note: Immediate from trace positivity; not stated as such.

items.label: Thm 7.2.1
items.statement: A Hermitian matrix is PSD (PD) iff all its eigenvalues are nonnegative (positive).

items.label: Cor 7.2.2
items.statement: Powers of a PSD matrix are PSD.

items.label: Cor 7.2.3
items.statement: A Hermitian strictly diagonally dominant matrix with positive diagonal is positive definite.
items.note: Candidate `gershgorin-diagonal-dominance`.

items.label: Cor 7.2.4
items.statement: A Hermitian matrix is PSD iff the nonzero coefficients of its characteristic polynomial alternate in sign.
items.note: Candidate `sylvester-criterion` (later part).

items.label: Thm 7.2.5
items.name: Sylvester's criterion
items.statement: Sylvester's criterion: nonnegative principal minors give PSD; positive leading (or trailing) principal minors give PD; positive first $n-1$ leading minors with $\det A\ge0$ give PSD.
items.note: Candidate `sylvester-criterion`; NLAlib has the neighbouring facts `posDef_iff_pivotSchur`, `IsLU.det_leadingSubmatrix`, `IsCholesky.det_eq_prod_sq`.

items.label: Thm 7.2.6
items.statement: A PSD matrix has a unique PSD $k$-th root $B$; $B$ is a real polynomial in $A$, has the same range, and is real when $A$ is.
items.note: Square root (and `nnrpow`) uniqueness in Mathlib's CFC; the polynomial and range clauses are not stated.

items.label: Thm 7.2.7
items.statement: A Hermitian $A$ is PSD iff $A=B^*B$; then $\ker A=\ker B$ and $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}B$; $A\succ0$ iff $B$ has full column rank.
items.note: Factorisation (real) in NLAlib, converse and rank in Mathlib; the null-space equality is not stated.

items.label: Cor 7.2.8
items.statement: A Hermitian matrix is PD iff it is *congruent to the identity.
items.note: Real symmetric: PD iff $A=LL^T$ with $L$ invertible.

items.label: Cor 7.2.9
items.name: Cholesky factorization
items.statement: Cholesky: a Hermitian matrix is PSD (PD) iff $A=LL^*$ with $L$ lower triangular with nonnegative (positive) diagonal; $L$ is unique when $A\succ0$ and real when $A$ is real.
items.note: Real case (the book notes $L$ can be taken real for real $A$).

items.label: Thm 7.2.10
items.statement: A Gram matrix $G=[\langle v_j,v_i\rangle]$ is PSD, is PD iff the $v_i$ are independent, and has rank $\dim\operatorname{span}\{v_i\}$.
items.note: Rank identity (c) not found in Mathlib.

items.label: Thm 7.3.1
items.name: Polar decomposition
items.statement: Polar decomposition: $A=PU$ or $A=UQ$ with $P=(AA^*)^{1/2}$, $Q=(A^*A)^{1/2}$ unique and $U$ with orthonormal rows/columns (unitary if square), unique when $A$ has full rank; real for real $A$.
items.note: NLAlib has the full-column-rank real case $Y=U(U^TY)$ with $U=Y(Y^TY)^{-1/2}$; general existence and uniqueness are candidate `polar-decomposition`.

items.label: Thm 7.3.2
items.name: Singular value decomposition
items.statement: SVD: $A=V\Sigma W^*$ with $V,W$ unitary and $\Sigma$ nonnegative diagonal, including the thin form $A=V_1\Sigma_rW_1^*$; real for real $A$.
items.note: Real matrices.

items.label: Thm 7.3.3
items.statement: The Hermitian dilation $\begin{bmatrix}0&A\\A^*&0\end{bmatrix}$ has eigenvalues $\pm\sigma_1,\dots,\pm\sigma_q$ and $|n-m|$ zeros.
items.note: NLAlib proves Hermitian-ness, $\mathcal H(A)^2=\operatorname{diag}(AA^*,A^*A)$ and $\lambda_{\max}=\|A\|$; the full eigenvalue list is not stated.

items.label: Cor 7.3.5
items.statement: Weyl and Mirsky for singular values: $|\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B)|\le\|A-B\|_2$ and $\sum_i(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2\le\|A-B\|_F^2$.
items.note: Real matrices.

items.label: Cor 7.3.6
items.statement: Deleting a row or column interlaces singular values: $\sigma_1\ge\hat\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\dots\ge\sigma_q\ge\hat\sigma_q$.
items.note: Candidate `singular-value-interlacing`.

items.label: Thm 7.3.8
items.statement: Min-max for singular values: $\sigma_k(A)=\min_{\dim S=m-k+1}\max_{x\in S}\|Ax\|/\|x\|=\max_{\dim S=k}\min_{x\in S}\|Ax\|/\|x\|$.
items.note: Stated as bound-plus-attainment pairs (real matrices).

items.label: Thm 7.3.11
items.statement: $A^*A=B^*B$ (with $p\le q$ rows) iff $B=VA$ for some $V$ with orthonormal columns; $V$ real if $A,B$ are.
items.note: Candidate `gram-equality-isometry` (later).

items.label: Ex 7.3.P7
items.name: Moore–Penrose inverse
items.statement: Moore–Penrose inverse: $A^\dagger=W\Sigma^\dagger V^*$ satisfies $AA^\dagger,A^\dagger A$ Hermitian, $AA^\dagger A=A$, $A^\dagger AA^\dagger=A^\dagger$, $(A^\dagger)^\dagger=A$, $A^\dagger=A^{-1}$ for nonsingular $A$, and is unique given these properties.
items.note: Real matrices. This is the precise location behind the atlas label §7.3 of `pseudoinverse`.

items.label: Thm 7.4.1.1
items.name: von Neumann's trace inequality
items.statement: von Neumann: $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(AB^*)\le\sum_i\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$.
items.note: Real matrices ($\operatorname{tr}A^TB=\langle A,B\rangle_F$).

items.label: Cor 7.4.1.3
items.statement: (a) $\|A-B\|_F^2\ge\sum_i(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2$; (b) $\sum_i\sigma_i(A)=\max\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(AU)$ over unitary $U$ (and two-sided forms).
items.note: (a) is NLAlib Mirsky; (b) (nuclear norm as a max over unitaries) is in the Ky Fan norms candidate.

items.label: Thm 7.4.1.4
items.statement: $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}A\le\sum_i\sigma_i(A)$, with equality iff the leading $q\times q$ block is PSD and all other entries vanish.
items.note: Trace bounded by nuclear norm; equality case is extra.

items.label: Cor 7.4.1.5
items.statement: Equality in $\|A-B\|_F^2\ge\sum(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2$ holds iff $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}AB^*=\sum\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$, and then $AB^*$ and $B^*A$ are PSD.
items.note: Candidate `orthogonal-procrustes` (later).

items.name: Eckart–Young (Frobenius)
items.statement: Nearest rank-$k$ matrix: $\min_{\operatorname{rank}B\le k}\|A-B\|_F^2=\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2$, attained by the truncated SVD (unique iff $\sigma_k>\sigma_{k+1}$); $\sigma_n$ is the Frobenius distance to the singular matrices.
items.note: Unnumbered subsection. Minimum value and attainment proved (Frobenius and spectral); the uniqueness clause is not stated.

items.statement: Least squares via SVD: $x=\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i^{-1}(v_i^*b)w_i$ minimises $\|Ax-b\|_2$ and has minimum norm among minimisers.
items.note: Unnumbered subsection; NLAlib states it through the Moore–Penrose inverse.

items.statement: The best Frobenius approximation of $A$ by $cU$ ($U$ unitary) is $(\tfrac1n\operatorname{tr}P)U_0$ from the polar form $A=PU_0$, with error $\sum(\sigma_i-\mu)^2$.
items.note: Unnumbered subsection; candidate `orthogonal-procrustes` (later).

items.name: Unitary Procrustes problem
items.statement: Unitary Procrustes: $\min_U\|A-UB\|_F$ is attained at the unitary polar factor of $AB^*$, with value $\|A\|_F^2-2\operatorname{tr}P+\|B\|_F^2$.
items.note: Unnumbered subsection; candidate `orthogonal-procrustes`.

items.statement: Two-sided rotation: $\min_{U,T}\|A-UBT\|_F^2=\sum(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2$, attained by aligning singular vectors.
items.note: Unnumbered subsection; candidate `orthogonal-procrustes` (later).

items.label: Def 7.4.7.1
items.name: Symmetric gauge function
items.statement: A symmetric gauge function is an absolute vector norm on $\mathbb C^q$ invariant under permutations.

items.label: Thm 7.4.7.2
items.name: von Neumann's gauge theorem
items.statement: Unitarily invariant norms on $M_{m,n}$ correspond bijectively to symmetric gauge functions via $\|A\|=g(\sigma(A))$.

items.label: Thm 7.4.8.4
items.name: Fan dominance theorem
items.statement: Fan dominance: $\|A\|\le\|B\|$ for every unitarily invariant norm iff $\|A\|_{[k]}\le\|B\|_{[k]}$ for every Ky Fan $k$-norm.

items.label: Thm 7.4.9.1
items.statement: For every unitarily invariant norm, $\|A-B\|\ge\|\Sigma(A)-\Sigma(B)\|$; consequently the truncated SVD is a best rank-$k$ approximation in every such norm.
items.note: Spectral and Frobenius instances proved; the all-unitarily-invariant-norm statement is in candidate `lidskii`.

items.label: Cor 7.4.9.3
items.name: Mirsky's theorem
items.statement: Mirsky: for Hermitian $A,B$ and any unitarily invariant norm, $\|\operatorname{diag}\lambda^\downarrow(A)-\operatorname{diag}\lambda^\downarrow(B)\|\le\|A-B\|$.

items.label: Thm 7.4.10.1
items.statement: A unitarily invariant norm on $M_n$ is submultiplicative iff $\|A\|\ge\sigma_1(A)$ for all $A$.
items.note: Low priority.

items.label: Cor 7.4.10.2
items.statement: Convex combinations of unitarily invariant matrix norms are unitarily invariant matrix norms.
items.note: Low priority.

items.label: Thm 7.4.11.1
items.statement: A unitarily invariant norm is absolute iff it is a positive multiple of the Frobenius norm.
items.note: Low priority remark.

items.name: Kantorovich and Wielandt inequalities
items.statement: Kantorovich: $(x^*Ax)(x^*A^{-1}x)\le\frac{(\lambda_1+\lambda_n)^2}{4\lambda_1\lambda_n}\|x\|^4$ for $A\succ0$; Wielandt: $|x^*Ay|^2\le\big(\frac{\lambda_1-\lambda_n}{\lambda_1+\lambda_n}\big)^2(x^*Ax)(y^*Ay)$ for orthogonal $x,y$; the two are equivalent.
items.note: Unnumbered subsection; candidate `kantorovich-inequality`.

items.label: Def 7.5.1
items.statement: The Hadamard (Schur) product $A\circ B=[a_{ij}b_{ij}]$.

items.label: Lem 7.5.2
items.statement: $x^*(A\circ B)y=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{diag}(\bar x)A\operatorname{diag}(y)B^T)$.

items.label: Thm 7.5.3
items.name: Schur product theorem
items.statement: Schur product theorem: $A,B\succeq0\Rightarrow A\circ B\succeq0$; if $A\succ0$ and $B\succeq0$ has positive diagonal then $A\circ B\succ0$; $A,B\succ0\Rightarrow A\circ B\succ0$.
items.note: (a) and (c) in Mathlib; (b) is in candidate `schur-product-inequalities`.

items.label: Thm 7.5.4
items.name: Moutard / Fejér
items.statement: Moutard–Fejér: $A$ is PSD iff $\operatorname{tr}(AB^T)=\sum a_{ij}b_{ij}\ge0$ for every PSD $B$ (the PSD cone is self-dual).
items.note: Candidate `psd-cone-self-dual`.

items.label: Thm 7.5.7
items.name: Weak minimum principle
items.statement: Weak minimum principle for an elliptic operator with $c<0$: no negative interior minimum or positive interior maximum; nonnegative boundary data force nonnegativity.
items.note: Elliptic PDE application (labelled "Weak minimum principle 7.5.7" in the text).

items.label: Thm 7.5.8
items.name: Fejér's uniqueness theorem
items.statement: Fejér uniqueness: the Dirichlet problem for such an elliptic operator has at most one classical solution.
items.note: Elliptic PDE application (labelled "Fejér's uniqueness theorem 7.5.8" in the text).

items.label: Thm 7.5.9
items.statement: Hadamard powers of a PSD matrix are PSD; $[f(a_{ij})]\succeq0$ for $f$ analytic with nonnegative coefficients; $[e^{a_{ij}}]\succeq0$, PD iff no two rows of $A$ coincide.
items.note: Candidate `schur-product-inequalities` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.6.1
items.statement: For Hermitian $A\succ0$ and $B$: $A=SS^*$, $B=S^{-*}\Lambda S^{-1}$ with $\Lambda$ real diagonal of the same inertia as $B$; for PSD $A,B$ a version with $A=S(I_r\oplus0)S^*$.
items.note: Candidate `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence`.

items.label: Cor 7.6.2
items.statement: If $A\succ0$ and $B$ Hermitian then $AB$ is diagonalizable with real eigenvalues (positive/nonnegative if $B$ is PD/PSD); for $A,B\succeq0$, $AB$ is diagonalizable with nonnegative eigenvalues.
items.note: Candidate `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence`.

items.label: Thm 7.6.3
items.statement: If $A\succeq0$ is singular and $B$ Hermitian, $AB$ is similar to $\Lambda\oplus N$ with $\Lambda$ real diagonal and $N$ a sum of $2\times2$ nilpotent Jordan blocks.
items.note: Jordan-form refinement over ℂ; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 7.6.4
items.statement: For $A\succ0$ and Hermitian $B$: $A=SS^*$, $B=S\Lambda S^*$ with $\Lambda$ the (real) eigenvalues of $A^{-1}B$; for PSD $A,B$ a version with $A=S(I_r\oplus0)S^*$.
items.note: Candidate `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence`.

items.label: Thm 7.6.5
items.statement: For $A\succ0$ and complex symmetric $B$: $A=SS^*$, $B=S\Sigma S^T$ with $\Sigma$ nonnegative diagonal.
items.note: Complex-symmetric (Takagi-type) congruence; no NLA consumer.

items.label: Thm 7.6.6
items.name: Concavity of log det
items.statement: $A\mapsto\log\det A$ is strictly concave on positive definite matrices.
items.note: Candidate `log-det-concavity`.

items.label: Cor 7.6.8
items.statement: For $A,B\succ0$ and $0<\alpha<1$: $\det(\alpha A+(1-\alpha)B)\ge(\det A)^\alpha(\det B)^{1-\alpha}$, with equality iff $A=B$.
items.note: Candidate `log-det-concavity`.

items.label: Thm 7.6.10
items.statement: $A\mapsto\operatorname{tr}A^{-1}$ is strictly convex on positive definite matrices.
items.note: Candidate `log-det-concavity`.

items.label: Def 7.7.1
items.name: Loewner partial order
items.statement: Loewner order: $A\succeq B$ if $A-B$ is PSD ($A\succ B$ if PD); it is a partial order.

items.label: Thm 7.7.2
items.statement: Congruence preserves the Loewner order ($S^*AS\succeq S^*BS$), strictly when $S$ has full column rank, iff when $S$ is nonsingular; $I\succeq S^*S$ iff $S$ is a contraction.
items.note: Contraction clause (d) not stated; NLAlib has the related `specNorm_le_iff_abs_dotProduct_mulVec_le`.

items.label: Thm 7.7.3
items.statement: For $A\succ0$, $B\succeq0$: $A\succeq B$ iff $\rho(A^{-1}B)\le1$ iff $B=A^{1/2}XA^{1/2}$ with $X$ a PSD contraction; $A^2\succeq B^2$ iff $\sigma_1(A^{-1}B)\le1$.
items.note: Candidate `loewner-relative-spectrum`.

items.label: Cor 7.7.4
items.statement: If $A\succeq B$: $B^{-1}\succeq A^{-1}$ (both PD), $A^{1/2}\succeq B^{1/2}$, $\lambda_i(A)\ge\lambda_i(B)$, $\operatorname{tr}A\ge\operatorname{tr}B$ (equality iff $A=B$), and $\det A\ge\det B$ when $B\succeq0$.
items.note: (a),(b) in Mathlib for C*-algebras (real-matrix form is atlas candidate `loewner-heinz-real`); (c),(d) in NLAlib without the trace equality case; (e) determinant monotonicity missing (candidate `loewner-relative-spectrum`).

items.label: Lem 7.7.6
items.statement: $\begin{bmatrix}I&X\\X^*&I\end{bmatrix}$ is PD (PSD) iff $X$ is a strict contraction (contraction).
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Thm 7.7.7
items.statement: For Hermitian $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{bmatrix}$, TFAE: $H\succ0$; $A\succ0$ and $C-B^*A^{-1}B\succ0$; $A,C\succ0$ with $\rho(B^*A^{-1}BC^{-1})<1$; $\sigma_1(A^{-1/2}BC^{-1/2})<1$; $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ with $X$ a strict contraction.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`. (a)⇔(b) is Mathlib `Matrix.PosDef.fromBlocks₁₁`.

items.label: Lem 7.7.8
items.statement: For singular PSD $A$, $(A+k^{-1}I)^{1/2}\to A^{1/2}$, and any sequence of contractions has a convergent subsequence with contraction limit.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`. (proof device; later)

items.label: Thm 7.7.9
items.statement: A Hermitian block matrix is PSD iff $A,C\succeq0$ and $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ for a contraction $X$.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`. The pseudoinverse Schur-complement form is the scaffold `generalized-schur-complement-psd`.

items.label: Cor 7.7.10
items.statement: Criteria for $\begin{bmatrix}A&I\\I&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ in terms of $A\succeq C^{-1}$, and $\begin{bmatrix}A&I\\I&A^{-1}\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ for $A\succ0$.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Thm 7.7.11
items.statement: For $A,C\succeq0$ TFAE: $(x^*Ax)(y^*Cy)\ge|x^*By|^2$; $x^*Ax+y^*Cy\ge2|x^*By|$; $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$; $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ with $X$ a contraction.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Cor 7.7.12
items.statement: For $A\succeq0$, $B$ Hermitian TFAE: $x^*Ax\ge|x^*Bx|$; the block $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&A\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$; $B=A^{1/2}XA^{1/2}$ with $X$ a Hermitian contraction.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Cor 7.7.13
items.statement: For $A,B\succeq0$ TFAE: $A\succeq B$; $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&A\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$; $B=A^{1/2}XA^{1/2}$ with $X$ a PSD contraction.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Cor 7.7.14
items.statement: If $x^*Ax\ge|x^*Bx|$ and $x^*Cx\ge|x^*Dx|$ for all $x$ (with $A,C\succeq0$) then $x^*(A\circ C)x\ge|x^*(B\circ D)x|$.
items.note: Candidate `schur-product-inequalities` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.7.15
items.statement: For $H\succ0$ and an index set $\alpha$: $(H^{-1})[\alpha]\succeq(H[\alpha])^{-1}$.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Thm 7.7.16
items.statement: For $A\succ0$ the block matrices $\begin{bmatrix}A&X\\X^*&X^*A^{-1}X\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}A&I\\I&A^{-1}\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}A&A\\A&A\end{bmatrix}$ (and related ones) are PSD and singular.
items.note: Candidate `psd-block-contraction`.

items.label: Thm 7.7.17
items.statement: For $A,B\succ0$: $A^{-1}\circ B^{-1}\succeq(A\circ B)^{-1}$, $A^{-1}\circ A^{-1}\succeq(A\circ A)^{-1}$, and $A^{-1}\circ A\succeq I\succeq(A^{-1}\circ A)^{-1}$.
items.note: Candidate `schur-product-inequalities` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.7.18
items.statement: For $A,B\succ0$: $\lambda_{\min}(A\circ B)\ge\max\{\lambda_{\min}(AB),\lambda_{\min}(AB^T)\}$.
items.note: Candidate `schur-product-inequalities` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.8.1
items.name: Hadamard's inequality
items.statement: Hadamard: for $A\succ0$, $\det A\le a_{11}\cdots a_{nn}$, with equality iff $A$ is diagonal.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`.

items.label: Cor 7.8.3
items.name: Hadamard's inequality
items.statement: For nonsingular $B$, $|\det B|\le\prod_i\|b_i\|_2$ (columns) and $\le\prod_i\|\beta_i\|_2$ (rows), with equality iff the columns (rows) are orthogonal.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`.

items.label: Thm 7.8.5
items.name: Fischer's inequality
items.statement: Fischer: for $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{bmatrix}\succ0$, $\det H\le\det A\det C$.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`.

items.label: Lem 7.8.8
items.statement: For $B\succ0$ and index sets with disjoint nonempty complements covering everything, $\det B[\alpha^c\cup\beta^c]\le\det B[\alpha^c]\det B[\beta^c]$.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`.

items.label: Thm 7.8.9
items.name: Koteljanskiĭ's inequality
items.statement: Koteljanskiĭ: for $A\succ0$, $\det A[\alpha\cup\beta]\det A[\alpha\cap\beta]\le\det A[\alpha]\det A[\beta]$.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`.

items.label: Thm 7.8.11
items.name: Szász's inequality
items.statement: Szász: the normalized products $P_k(A)^{1/\binom{n-1}{k-1}}$ of $k\times k$ principal minors are nonincreasing in $k$.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`. (later)

items.label: Lem 7.8.15
items.statement: For PSD $A=\begin{bmatrix}a_{11}&x^*\\x&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}$, subtracting $\alpha(A)=\det A/\det A_{22}$ (or 0) from $a_{11}$ leaves a PSD matrix.
items.note: Candidate `hadamard-fischer-inequalities`. (helper for Oppenheim; later)

items.label: Thm 7.8.16
items.name: Oppenheim–Schur inequalities
items.statement: Oppenheim–Schur: for PSD $A,B$, $\max\{a_{11}\cdots a_{nn}\det B,\ b_{11}\cdots b_{nn}\det A\}\le\det(A\circ B)$, and a sharper two-term inequality.
items.note: Candidate `schur-product-inequalities` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.8.19
items.name: Ostrowski–Taussky inequality
items.statement: Ostrowski–Taussky: if $H\succ0$ then $\det H\le|\det(H+iK)|$, with equality iff $K=0$.
items.note: Candidate `psd-hermitian-part` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.8.21
items.name: Minkowski's determinant inequality
items.statement: Minkowski: for $A,B\succ0$, $(\det A)^{1/n}+(\det B)^{1/n}\le(\det(A+B))^{1/n}$, with equality iff $A=cB$.
items.note: Candidate `log-det-concavity`.

items.label: Thm 7.8.24
items.statement: For $n\ge2$ and $H\succ0$: $\det H+|\det K|\le|\det(H+iK)|$, with stated equality cases.
items.note: Candidate `psd-hermitian-part` (later).

items.label: Thm 7.8.27
items.name: Fan's determinant inequality
items.statement: Fan: for $H\succ0$, $(\det H)^{2/n}+|\det K|^{2/n}\le|\det(H+iK)|^{2/n}$, equality iff the eigenvalues of $H^{-1}K$ have equal moduli.
items.note: Candidate `psd-hermitian-part` (later).

items.label: Prop 8.1.8
items.statement: $|Ax|\le|A||x|$ entrywise; equality $|Ax|=A|x|$ for nonnegative $A$ with a positive row forces $x$ to be a unimodular multiple of $|x|$; $Ax=|A|x$ with $x>0$ forces $A=|A|$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.1.18
items.statement: If $B\ge0$ and $|A|\le B$ entrywise then $\rho(A)\le\rho(|A|)\le\rho(B)$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.19
items.statement: For $0\le A\le B$ entrywise, $\rho(A)\le\rho(B)$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.20
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$: principal submatrices have smaller spectral radius, $\max_ia_{ii}\le\rho(A)$, and $\rho(A)>0$ if some $a_{ii}>0$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.1.21
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$, $\rho(A)\le$ the maximum row sum and the maximum column sum, with equality when all row (column) sums are equal.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.1.22
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$, the minimum row sum $\le\rho(A)\le$ the maximum row sum (and likewise for columns).
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.25
items.statement: A nonnegative matrix with all row sums (or all column sums) positive has $\rho(A)>0$; in particular irreducible nonnegative matrices with $n\ge2$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.1.26
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$ and positive $x$: $\min_i x_i^{-1}\sum_ja_{ij}x_j\le\rho(A)\le\max_i x_i^{-1}\sum_ja_{ij}x_j$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.29
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$ and positive $x$: $\alpha x\le Ax\le\beta x$ implies $\alpha\le\rho(A)\le\beta$ (strict versions too).
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.30
items.statement: A positive eigenvector of a nonnegative matrix belongs to $\rho(A)$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.31
items.statement: If nonnegative $A$ has a positive eigenvector, $\rho(A)$ is a max-min and a min-max of the ratios $x_i^{-1}(Ax)_i$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.1.33
items.statement: If nonnegative $A$ has a positive eigenvector, the row sums of $A^m$ are within a fixed ratio of $\rho(A)^m$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.2.1
items.statement: For positive $A$, an eigenpair with $|\lambda|=\rho(A)$ has $|x|>0$ and $A|x|=\rho(A)|x|$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.2.2
items.statement: A positive matrix has positive right and left eigenvectors for $\rho(A)$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.2.3
items.statement: For positive $A$, an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of modulus $\rho(A)$ is a unimodular multiple of a positive vector.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.2.4
items.statement: For positive $A$, every eigenvalue other than $\rho(A)$ has modulus $<\rho(A)$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.2.5
items.statement: For positive $A$, $\rho(A)$ has geometric multiplicity one.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.2.6
items.statement: A positive matrix has a unique normalized (sum-one) eigenvector for $\rho(A)$, and it is positive (the Perron vector).
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.2.7
items.statement: For positive $A$, $\rho(A)$ is algebraically simple and $(\rho(A)^{-1}A)^m\to xy^T$ (Perron vectors).
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.2.8
items.name: Perron's theorem
items.statement: Perron's theorem for positive matrices: $\rho(A)>0$ is an algebraically simple dominant eigenvalue with a positive Perron vector and the power limit $xy^T$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.2.9
items.statement: Fan: if $B\ge0$ and $b_{ij}\ge|a_{ij}|$ off the diagonal, every eigenvalue of $A$ lies in $\bigcup_i\{z:|z-a_{ii}|\le\rho(B)-b_{ii}\}$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.3.1
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$, $\rho(A)$ is an eigenvalue with a nonnegative eigenvector.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.3.2
items.statement: For nonnegative $A$ and nonnegative nonzero $x$, $Ax\ge\alpha x$ implies $\rho(A)\ge\alpha$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.3.3
items.statement: Collatz–Wielandt: $\rho(A)=\max_{x\ge0,x\ne0}\min_{x_i\ne0}x_i^{-1}(Ax)_i$ for nonnegative $A$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.3.4
items.statement: If nonnegative $A$ has a positive right or left eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda\ge0$, then $\lambda=\rho(A)$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.3.5
items.statement: If nonnegative $A$ has a positive left eigenvector, then $Ax\ge\rho(A)x$ forces equality, and the peripheral eigenvalues are semisimple.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.4.1
items.statement: Nonnegative $A$ is irreducible iff $(I+A)^{n-1}>0$.
items.note: Mathlib states a power-positivity criterion for irreducibility; the exact $(I+A)^{n-1}$ form is not stated.

items.label: Lem 8.4.2
items.statement: The eigenvalues of $I+A$ are $\lambda_i+1$; $\rho(I+A)\le\rho(A)+1$ with equality for nonnegative $A$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.4.3
items.statement: If nonnegative $A$ has $A^m>0$, then $\rho(A)$ is the unique, positive, algebraically simple eigenvalue of maximum modulus.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.4.4
items.name: Perron–Frobenius theorem
items.statement: Perron–Frobenius for irreducible nonnegative matrices: $\rho(A)>0$ is an algebraically simple eigenvalue with positive left and right eigenvectors.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.4.5
items.statement: If $A\ge|B|$ with $A$ irreducible nonnegative and $\rho(A)=\rho(B)$, then $B=e^{i\varphi}DAD^{-1}$ for a diagonal unitary $D$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.4.6
items.statement: An irreducible nonnegative matrix with $k$ peripheral eigenvalues is similar to $e^{2\pi ip/k}A$, and its peripheral Jordan structure is rotation invariant.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.4.7
items.statement: If an irreducible nonnegative matrix has $k>1$ peripheral eigenvalues, its diagonal is zero, as is that of $A^m$ for $k\nmid m$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Def 8.5.0
items.statement: A nonnegative matrix is primitive if it is irreducible with a unique eigenvalue of maximum modulus.
items.note: Mathlib defines primitivity via a positive power; equivalence with this definition is Thm 8.5.2.

items.label: Thm 8.5.1
items.statement: For primitive $A$, $(\rho(A)^{-1}A)^m\to xy^T$, a positive rank-one matrix.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.5.2
items.statement: A nonnegative matrix is primitive iff some power is positive.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.5.3
items.statement: An irreducible nonnegative matrix is primitive iff all cycle-length gcds of its digraph equal one.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.5.4
items.statement: An irreducible nonnegative matrix with positive diagonal satisfies $A^{n-1}>0$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.5.5
items.statement: Powers of a primitive matrix are primitive.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.5.6
items.statement: A primitive matrix has $A^k>0$ for some $k\le(n-1)n^n$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.5.7
items.statement: If the shortest cycle of a primitive matrix has length $s$, then $A^{n+s(n-2)}>0$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Cor 8.5.8
items.name: Wielandt's theorem
items.statement: Wielandt: $A\ge0$ is primitive iff $A^{n^2-2n+2}>0$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.5.9
items.statement: An irreducible nonnegative matrix with $d$ positive diagonal entries has $A^{2n-d-1}>0$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Thm 8.6.1
items.statement: For irreducible nonnegative $A$, the Cesàro means of $(\rho(A)^{-1}A)^m$ converge to $xy^T$.
items.note: Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative matrices; out of scope for this library.

items.label: Lem 8.7.1
items.statement: A doubly stochastic matrix other than $I$ has a positive diagonal along some non-identity permutation.
items.note: Step in the book's proof of Birkhoff's theorem, which Mathlib proves by another route.

items.label: Thm 8.7.2
items.name: Birkhoff's theorem
items.statement: Birkhoff: doubly stochastic matrices are exactly convex combinations of permutation matrices (at most $n^2-n+1$ of them).
items.note: The Carathéodory count $N\le n^2-n+1$ is not stated.

items.label: Cor 8.7.4
items.statement: A convex (concave) function on the doubly stochastic matrices attains its maximum (minimum) at a permutation matrix.
items.note: Immediate combination; not stated as one lemma.

items.label: Lem 8.7.5
items.statement: Every doubly substochastic matrix is entrywise dominated by a doubly stochastic matrix.
items.note: Proof device for von Neumann's trace theorem in this book; NLAlib proves that theorem by another route.

items.label: Thm 8.7.6
items.name: von Neumann's trace theorem
items.statement: von Neumann: for square $A,B$, $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(AB)\le\sum_i\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$.
items.note: Real matrices; $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\langle A^T,B\rangle_F$ and $\sigma(A^T)=\sigma(A)$.
